papers.title: Mucosal Small Cell Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Gallbladder With Extraregional Lymph Node Metastasis: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Gallbladder small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (SCNEC) is a rare and highly aggressive malignancy, and an optimal treatment strategy has not been established. We report a case of mucosal gallbladder SCNEC with extraregional lymph node metastasis that responded well to chemotherapy. A 69-year-old woman presented with severe epigastric pain and inflammatory findings. Ultrasonography, endoscopic ultrasonography, and computed tomography revealed a 40 mm gallbladder mass and enlarged lymph nodes in the hepatoduodenal ligament. Because inflammation and pain could not be controlled by conservative treatment and endoscopic gallbladder drainage was unsuccessful, emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed SCNEC with a Ki-67 index of 80%. Although continuous tumor invasion was limited to the mucosal layer and the tumor was classified as T1a, lymphatic invasion was present. Postoperative positron emission tomography and octreotide scintigraphy revealed metastases in the hepatoduodenal ligament and extraregional perisplenic artery lymph nodes. Further surgical resection was not performed, and chemotherapy with cisplatin and irinotecan was initiated. After six cycles, the hepatoduodenal ligament lymph node decreased from 31 mm to 13 mm, and the perisplenic artery lymph node disappeared, resulting in a partial response. No disease progression was observed during the 12-month postoperative follow-up period. This case suggests that gallbladder SCNEC may have metastatic potential even when the primary tumor is limited to the mucosal layer. Careful systemic staging is important, and platinum-based chemotherapy may be effective for metastatic disease.

papers.title: Widespread Cutaneous Metastases as the Primary Presentation of an Occult Neuroendocrine Tumour of Unknown Primary.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous metastases from neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are extremely rare even in advanced disease and may rarely be the initial presentation of an occult primary tumour. We describe a woman in her late 30s who presented with slowly growing skin lesions over a period of two years without associated systemic symptoms. She later developed abdominal discomfort, prompting hospital assessment. Clinical examination revealed extensive cutaneous nodules and a palpable abdominal mass. Imaging demonstrated widespread metastatic disease with multiple soft tissue deposits involving the liver, brain, and other deep organs. Histopathological examination of skin biopsies confirmed a grade 3 metastatic neuroendocrine tumour (NET) with a possible bronchial primary origin. The patient received systemic chemotherapy in addition to palliative radiotherapy for symptomatic lesions. Despite treatment, her condition progressively deteriorated due to the extensive disease burden, and management was subsequently redirected towards best supportive care with a focus on symptom control. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by the variable cutaneous presentations of NENs, which can often be mistaken for benign growths without a high index of suspicion. This emphasises the importance of early recognition and biopsy of suspicious skin lesions.

papers.title: Peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma of unknown primary with markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein: a case report.
papers.abstract: Peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma(NEC) is primarily metastatic, with primary cases being exceedingly rare. The relationship between alpha-fetoprotein(AFP) and neuroendocrine carcinoma remains unclear. In this report, we present a patient with peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma who exhibited significantly elevated AFP levels. Extensive evaluation revealed no obvious primary site outside the peritoneum; however, occult gastrointestinal origin could not be entirely excluded. The tumor was thus classified as NEC of unknown primary, with a presumed primary peritoneal origin. The findings from this case suggest that markedly elevated AFP may be associated with aggressive tumor behavior and could serve as a potential marker for monitoring disease activity in peritoneal NECs, a hypothesis that warrants further investigation. A 51-year-old man with massive ascites and elevated AFP levels was admitted to the hospital. Liver enhanced magnetic resonance imaging and gastrointestinal endoscopy did not reveal any space-occupying lesions, while abdominal puncture did not detect tumor cells. The patient's whole-body PET-CT revealed extensive peritoneal thickening and increased FDG metabolism. Subsequent laparoscopic exploration revealed numerous nodules and masses of varying sizes with a firm texture in the greater omentum, small intestine surface, mesentery, and parietal peritoneum. Immunohistochemistry of the omentum demonstrated positive results for AE1/AE3, Syn, CgA, and AFP, leading to a final diagnosis of large cell NEC of unknown primary, with a presumed primary peritoneal origin. Due to the presence of multiple peritoneal nodules, radical surgery was not feasible, and EP combined with camrelizumab was initiated. AFP levels showed an overall progressive increase, peaking at 5315 ng/mL on May 25, with a slight subsequent decline to 4948.4 ng/mL on June 20. Unfortunately, the patient discontinued chemotherapy after two cycles due to severe nausea and vomiting; he subsequently succumbed to the disease. We propose the hypothesis that dynamic changes in AFP levels could reflect tumor burden and treatment response in a subset of AFP-producing NECs. However, this hypothesis requires validation in larger cohort studies. It is also important to distinguish its potential role as a monitoring biomarker from an established prognostic biomarker.

papers.title: Living Donor Liver Transplantation for Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide-Secreting Tumors with Watery Diarrhea, Hypokalemia, and Achlorhydria Syndrome Resulting from Transformation of a Nonfunctional Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor with Multiple Liver Metastases: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PNENs) are a rare subtype of neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs), some of which cause characteristic clinical syndromes due to hormone hypersecretion. Vasoactive intestinal peptide-secreting tumors (VIPomas) produce vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) and are associated with watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, and achlorhydria (WDHA) syndrome, often leading to severe treatment-refractory symptoms. Although liver transplantation (LT) is regarded as a promising option for unresectable, liver-limited NENs, studies focusing on VIPoma remain limited, as do reports of transformation from nonfunctional pancreatic NENs (PNENs) to VIPoma. Furthermore, to the best of our knowledge, no cases have described progression to LT after such a transformation. Therefore, we report this case. A 65-year-old woman with nonfunctional PNEN G2 and multiple liver metastases underwent multimodal treatment including a multi-kinase inhibitor, somatostatin analogs, a mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors, and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). During treatment, the tumor acquired VIP-secreting capacity and transformed into a VIPoma, resulting in WDHA syndrome characterized by intractable watery diarrhea, severe electrolyte imbalance, and metabolic acidosis. Because neither conservative management nor debulking surgery achieved adequate symptom control, and no extrahepatic disease was identified, living donor LT (LDLT) was performed. After transplantation, the diarrhea resolved promptly, and no recurrence has been observed 1 year post-transplantation. We report a rare case in which a nonfunctional PNEN transformed into a VIPoma during the clinical course, leading to severe WDHA syndrome. LDLT for liver-limited disease may represent an effective therapeutic option for both tumor control and symptom relief in carefully selected patients.

papers.title: Gastric Glomus Tumor Mimicking a Neuroendocrine Tumor: A Case Report Highlighting Diagnostic Pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Gastric glomus tumors (GGTs) are rare mesenchymal neoplasms arising from the modified smooth muscle cells of the glomus body. Their subepithelial location and pronounced hypervascularity overlap considerably with gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) on imaging and in small biopsy specimens, making an accurate preoperative diagnosis challenging; as a result, such lesions are frequently diagnosed after surgical resection. A 38-year-old asymptomatic woman was found to have a 25-mm well-circumscribed, hypervascular submucosal lesion with a small central depression and minute ulceration in the upper gastric body during a routine health-screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD). Endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) demonstrated a heterogeneous hypoechoic mass arising from the third sonographic layer without evidence of muscularis propria invasion. Contrast-enhanced CT showed a hypervascular lesion with no regional lymphadenopathy or distant metastasis. Conventional forceps biopsies targeting the minute ulceration, evaluated with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining alone, were interpreted as consistent with a NET, leading to a provisional diagnosis of a type III gastric NET. Because of the diagnostic uncertainty surrounding the NET diagnosis, and because the EUS and CT showed no evidence of deep or nodal spread, the patient underwent laparoscopic and endoscopic cooperative surgery (LECS) with a local full-thickness gastric resection rather than upfront gastrectomy with lymphadenectomy, and the defect was repaired through a protective mini-laparotomy. Definitive histopathology demonstrated uniform round-to-spindle cells arranged in a perivascular sheet pattern within a myxoid stroma. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) showed focal positivity for α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) and negativity for KIT (CD117), CD34, chromogranin A, synaptophysin, desmin, and the S-100 protein, confirming a GGT. All surgical margins were negative, and no recurrence has been observed over 5 years of follow-up. A GGT must be included in the differential diagnosis of hypervascular gastric subepithelial lesions (SELs), including those with a nested, NET-like architecture. H&E staining alone is insufficient for a definitive diagnosis; direct communication with the pathologist and comprehensive IHC profiling are indispensable. LECS is a favorable and effective organ-preserving strategy for localized gastric SELs when the diagnosis remains uncertain despite the preoperative evaluation.

papers.title: Extensive bilateral adrenal calcification in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome-associated pheochromocytoma.
Endoscopic diagnosis and management of biliary neuroendocrine tumor with prior Roux-en-Y choledochojejunostomy: a case report.
papers.abstract: A 74-year-old woman with a previous Roux-en-Y choledochojejunostomy presented with biliary sepsis, Escherichia coli bacteremia, and a left-sided intrahepatic biliary stricture. Initial management included percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography with external biliary drainage. Colonoscope-directed cholangioscopy enabled biopsies and balloon dilatation because of the colonoscope's suitable length and channel diameter. Histology revealed a poorly differentiated neuroendocrine tumor of the bile duct. Surgical resection was abandoned intraoperatively because of peritoneal metastases. Following chemotherapy, the patient re-presented with biliary sepsis. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography using a pediatric colonoscope allowed placement of an uncovered self-expandable metal stent across the intrahepatic stricture. The patient underwent lutetium therapy and was clinically stable at 12-month follow-up. This case highlights biliary neuroendocrine tumor as a rare cause of stricture and demonstrates the utility of colonoscope-directed cholangioscopy and endoscopic retrograde cholangiography for diagnosis and management.

papers.title: Pseudo-cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea following endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal surgery for PitNET: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Pseudo-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) rhinorrhea, defined as non-CSF nasal discharge mimicking true CSF leakage, is a rare but clinically significant complication that may prompt unnecessary aggressive treatment. We report a case of a 64-year-old man who developed positional clear nasal discharge after endoscopic endonasal resection of recurrent pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). Glucose oxidase testing was negative, and imaging demonstrated intact skull base reconstruction. Nasal endoscopy revealed bilateral crusting and purulent secretions without evidence of CSF leak. The condition was diagnosed as vasomotor rhinitis. Conservative management-including nasal debridement, antibiotic therapy, topical corticosteroids, and saline irrigation-led to complete symptom resolution. This case underscores the importance of differentiating pseudo-CSF rhinorrhea from true CSF rhinorrhea to avoid invasive interventions.

papers.title: Methylation profiling reveals epigenetic programs associated with chr18 loss in small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SI-NETs) are characterized by a low mutational burden and limited recurrent driver mutations, suggesting that other mechanisms contribute to tumor development. One of the most frequent genomic alterations in SI-NETs is loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 18 (chr18del), which defines a major molecular subtype. However, the epigenetic consequences of this event remain poorly understood. In this study, we used long-read whole-genome sequencing to characterize genome-wide DNA methylation patterns in twelve primary tumors. Native methylation detection and copy-number profiling enabled stratification of tumors according to chromosome 18 status and direct comparison of epigenetic states between chr18del and non-chr18del (diploid) tumors. Chr18del tumors displayed widespread hypomethylation relative to diploid tumors, while chromosome 18 showed spatially structured regional methylation differences, including localized regions of increased methylation. Cross-platform validation using an independent Illumina EPIC methylation cohort confirmed the direction and distribution of many methylation events. Integration with the corresponding transcriptomic dataset revealed that a subset of methylation changes was associated with differential gene expression consistent with established promoter- and gene-body methylation models. Functional categorization of these methylation states revealed regulatory patterns linked to neuronal signaling, intracellular signaling cascades, and interactions with the extracellular matrix. Together, these findings support an association between chromosome 18 status and widespread methylation differences that extend beyond the affected chromosome and are linked to transcriptional programs relevant to neuroendocrine tumor biology.

papers.title: In reply to the comment on "Role of extracellular volume fraction determined by dual-layer spectral detector CT in predicting the tumor grade of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms".
Biogenic amines as neuroendocrine tumor markers: limitations and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Biogenic amines and their metabolites are central biochemical markers in the diagnosis and management of catecholamine-producing neuroendocrine tumors, including pheochromocytoma, paraganglioma, and neuroblastoma. Despite decades of clinical use, their wider implementation remains limited by substantial physiological variability, pre-analytical influences, and methodological heterogeneity across laboratories. The transition from colorimetric and immunoassay-based techniques to liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry has markedly improved analytical sensitivity and specificity. The multiplexing capacity of modern mass spectrometric platforms has enabled comprehensive quantification of biogenic amine profiles, thereby increasing diagnostic sensitivity in tumor subtypes in which individual biomarkers exhibit limited performance. Increasing attention has been given to dopamine derived metabolites, especially 3-methoxytyramine, which is associated with MYCN-related tumor biology and unfavorable clinical outcomes in neuroblastoma and selected paraganglioma subtypes. However, the analytical complexity of mass spectrometric approaches, together with the absence of full metrological traceability, continues to limit inter-laboratory comparability. In this review, we critically evaluate the analytical evolution of biogenic amine testing, the principal pre-analytical and methodological determinants that influence the interpretation of results, and current efforts to improve harmonization. Particular emphasis is placed on the potential of biogenic amines as prognostic biomarkers and on the need to integrate expanded biogenic amine profiling into clinically robust, comparable diagnostic approaches that may advance precision oncology.

papers.title: The Use and Utility of Preoperative Somatostatin Receptor-Based Imaging in Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: Contemporary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEPNET) management guidelines recommend routine use of functional imaging preoperatively, but there are few data highlighting trends in functional imaging adoption. This report reviews 24 years of neuroendocrine tumor (NET) experience to describe changes in rates of preoperative functional imaging use and highlights performance differences between functional imaging types in small bowel NETs (SBNET) and pancreatic NETs (PNETs). A retrospective single-institution study from 2000 to 2023 identified patients with SBNETs and PNETs treated with surgical resection, cytoreduction, or both who underwent preoperative functional imaging. The primary measurements were frequency of functional imaging use and location of metastases identified on preoperative imaging. The study included 392 SBNET and 208 PNET patients. Preoperative functional imaging was performed for 248 (63.3%) SBNET patients (158 somatostatin receptor [SSTR] positron emission tomography [PET] and 90 Octreoscan) and 113 (54.3%) PNET patients (47 SSTR PET and 66 Octreoscan). There was a significant positive trend over time in functional imaging use in SBNET patients, with an approximate 2.5% yearly increase (p < 0.01) but no significant change in PNET patients during the course of the study (p = 0.82). At presentation, 82.3% (204/248) of the SBNET patients and 54.9% (62/113) of the PNET patients had metastatic disease. Compared with Octreoscan, SSTR PET more frequently identified bone and retroperitoneal nodal metastases. Rates of functional imaging use in SBNET patients but not in PNET patients increased significantly during the last 24 years. Patients with SBNETs and PNETs frequently presented with metastatic disease, and SSTR-based functional imaging was extremely helpful in identifying distant disease, intra-operative planning, and further management.

papers.title: Transcatheter Adrenal Arterial Embolization for Life-Threatening Pheochromocytoma Crisis.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma crisis is a life-threatening endocrine emergency frequently complicated by Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) and cardiogenic shock. Hemodynamic stabilization is difficult to achieve with medical therapy alone, and emergency surgery carries high perioperative mortality. A 50-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, de Winter sign, basal-type TTS, and refractory cardiogenic shock with extreme blood pressure lability. Imaging revealed a 6.5 × 4.7 cm adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Despite optimal medical treatment, hemodynamic stability could not be achieved. Urgent transcatheter adrenal arterial embolization (TAAE) was performed as rescue therapy with sustained hemodynamic stabilization thereafter. After 1 month of alpha-blockade preparation, elective adrenalectomy was completed uneventfully. At the 1-year follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic with normal cardiac function and no tumor recurrence. In this case, TAAE served as a minimally invasive bridging measure for refractory pheochromocytoma crisis. The staged strategy combining TAAE with delayed elective adrenalectomy was associated with a favorable outcome. Extreme blood-pressure lability in a patient with TTS should prompt evaluation for occult pheochromocytoma. Urgent TAAE may serve as an effective bridge to delayed elective adrenalectomy for refractory pheochromocytoma crisis.

papers.title: [Paragangliomas of the head and neck. Epidemiology and diagnosis].
papers.abstract: Head and neck tumors cross several clinical specialties. Diagnostic and treatment approaches vary significantly depending on specialty, and there is no a unified diagnostic standard for paragangliomas in these areas. In this report, we summarize available data on these tumors and present own patient evaluation protocol. To systematize modern information on epidemiology, pathogenesis and diagnosis of paragangliomas. We present literature review and retrospective analysis of instrumental and laboratory data of patients with head and neck paragangliomas. We analyzed modern diagnostic methods: imaging (Doppler ultrasound, CT, MRI, PET CT), biochemical (catecholamines and their metabolites), and molecular genetic (mutation testing) tests. Advantages and limitations of each method were identified. We also present optimal algorithms for their combination for early and accurate disease detection. This analysis systematized the approach to diagnostic algorithm for patients with head and neck paragangliomas. The capabilities of modern imaging methods allow for identification of potentially malignant and familial forms of disease, which are fundamentally different from sporadic forms. Available data underlie a differentiated approach to treatment strategy. This positively impacts treatment outcomes. This aspect will be discussed in the second part of the article.

papers.title: [Desmoplastic infantile gangliogliomas/astrocytomas: clinical course, surgery and morphological diagnosis].
papers.abstract: Desmoplastic infantile gangliogliomas (DIG) and astrocytomas (DIA) are benign brain tumors in infants. They comprise 1.3-15.8% of tumors in infants / young children and 0.5-1% in older children. In the latest 2021 WHO classification of the CNS tumors, DIG and DIA are included in the group of neuronal and glioneuronal tumors and considered as a single entity within this group despite some morphological differences. In this classification, they are classified as low-grade tumors (Grade I). However, several cases of DIG/DIA with aggressive behavior were described in the literature. To analyze 2 different clinical courses of DIG/DIA with various neuroimaging signs, intraoperative situations and morphological pictures with review of appropriate literature. Two main courses of disease in children with DIG/DIA are presented. The first one is characterized by rapid growth of tumor, its large size upon diagnosis with progressive intracranial hypertension. The second type includes slow growth, small size, and only focal neurological symptoms. DIG/DIA are rare tumors and most often diagnosed in the first 2 years of life. They have some common neuroradiological and histological features with malignant brain tumors (malignant glioma of infancy, PNET), but another prognosis. Aggressive clinical course, rapid tumor growth, MR-based differential diagnosis involving multiple histological forms and histopathological findings potentially mimicking malignant tumor complicate differential diagnosis, as it was in the second case. Probably, such an aggressive clinical course is associated with significant spread of neoplastic astrocytic and neuronal components with foci of primitive embryonic cell complexes with increased proliferative index. Surgery is preferable. Difficult resection of these tumors is associated with rich vascularity, high risk of fatal bleeding, no border with normal brain tissue, and tendency to infiltrate functionally significant structures of the central nervous system.

papers.title: [Dinamic of biochemical parameters in patients with vestibular schwannoma in perioperative period].
papers.abstract: The correlation of cardiovascular and humoral responses to neurosurgical trauma near the cranial nerves is interesting for predicting of the postoperative period. To study the correlation between cardiovascular and humoral responses to neurosurgical intervention for vestibular schwannoma (VS) by comparing changes in blood parameters during the intraoperative period. The study included data of 92 neurosurgical patients who underwent surgery for vestibular schwannoma. The patients were divided into two groups: 46 patients without vegetative reactions during tumor removal; 43 patients who had type 1 vegetative reactions; 3 patients had type 2 vegetative reactions, but the last group for the small number of patients was excluded from statistical analysis. Biochemical indicators were studied, including glucose, lactate, urea, uric acid, total protein, albumin, total bilirubin, cholesterol, creatinine, creatine kinase, myoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), amylase, iron, C-reactive protein (CRP), sodium, and potassium at various stages of the perioperative period. The level of uric acid in the plasma of patients in group 1 on the first postoperative day was higher than in patients in group 2. Creatine kinase levels increased in all groups. C-reactive protein exceeded the reference values 4-5 times on the first postoperative day. Dynamics of changes in uric acid, CRP, glucose, and lactate levels are the result of the body's humoral response to multifactorial influences during neurosurgical intervention, most pronounced in combination with type 2 vegetative reactions, which are a consequence of hypercatecholaminemia.

papers.title: Merkel Cell Polyomavirus and DNA Damage Response.
papers.abstract: Cellular DNA is constantly exposed to endogenous and exogenous genotoxic factors causing mutations. Therefore, safeguarding the integrity of the human genome is a conditio sine qua non for normal cell function. To maintain genomic integrity, complex multiprotein networks, known as DNA damage response (DDR) signaling pathways, sense DNA lesions and repair mistakes or induce cell death when extensive unrepairable damage has occurred. Two of the major DDR pathways are the ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) and ataxia-telangiectasia and Rad3-related (ATR) cascades. The ATM pathway primarily responds to double-strand breaks, whereas the ATR cascade is activated by single-stranded DNA and mediates the response to replication stress. One of the exogenous factors that can induce DNA aberrations and trigger the ATM and ATR pathways is viral infection. This review focuses on current knowledge regarding the interaction between Merkel cell polyomavirus, a major etiological risk factor of Merkel cell carcinoma, and the ATM and ATR pathways and the effect on viral replication and virus-induced oncogenesis. The review elaborates on the role of the viral oncoproteins large T antigen and small t antigen in DDR interaction. Possible therapies targeting DDR in Merkel cell carcinoma and gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms of Merkel cell polyomavirus-triggered ATM and ATR pathway activation are discussed.

papers.title: Pulmonary Carcinoid Tumors (Lung Carcinoids): Current Concepts in Diagnosis and Management.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary carcinoid tumors are rare lung neuroendocrine neoplasms with diverse clinical behavior, ranging from indolent localized disease to metastatic progression. Diagnosis relies on histopathology but may be supplemented by immunohistochemical markers such as Ki-67. Recent molecular and multi-omic studies reveal substantial heterogeneity, identifying molecularly defined subgroups and highly proliferative carcinoids with aggressive behavior. Management includes surgical resection for localized disease and systemic therapies for advanced cases, such as somatostatin analogs, targeted agents, peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, and chemotherapy. While emerging molecular classifications and biomarker-driven strategies hold significant promise, current management of advanced pulmonary carcinoids relies heavily on extrapolated data from mixed neuroendocrine cohorts, underscoring the urgent need for prospective thoracic-dedicated trials to validate these paradigms in clinical practice. Emerging biomarker-driven trial designs and integrated precision medicine approaches offer opportunities to optimize therapy and improve outcomes in this rare tumor type.

papers.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Data in Metastatic Melanoma with Pre-Existing Autoimmune Disease: A Real World Experience.
papers.abstract: Patients with pre-existing autoimmune disease (AID) are underrepresented in trials of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). We retrospectively compared 41 patients with stage IV melanoma and pre-existing AID with 162 contemporaneous controls without AID who received ICI treatment between November 2016 and April 2023. In the AID and control cohorts, respectively, the objective response rates were 46.3% and 32.7%, and the disease control rates were 80.5% and 51.2%. Treatment interruption attributed to worsening of the baseline AID was recorded in 11/41 patients, while 13/41 interrupted treatment because of toxicity distinct from the baseline AID. The full cohort contributed 114 progression-free survival (PFS) events and 92 deaths. In models adjusted for age, sex, ICI regimen and M category, AID was associated with PFS (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.24-0.99; p = 0.046), whereas the association with overall survival (OS) was not statistically significant (adjusted HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.29-1.34; p = 0.232). These findings support the feasibility of ICI therapy in carefully selected patients with clinically stable AID, while the observational design and residual confounding require cautious interpretation of comparative outcomes.

papers.title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of Russian Patients with von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome (VHLS) is an autosomal dominant hereditary cancer disease caused by germline mutations in the VHL tumor suppressor gene and characterized by clinical heterogeneity and phenotype-genotype associations. We studied the VHL gene in 535 Russian patients referred for VHLS diagnostics using Sanger sequencing, multiplex ligase-dependent probe amplification, and, in some cases, high-throughput sequencing. A total of 177 causative VHL variants were identified, including 129 point mutations and 48 extended deletions. Missense variants were the most frequent (60.3%) and predominantly localized at codons 167, 88, and 78. Approximately 88% of the analyzed missense variants and in-frame indels led to changes directly at the HIF-α- and ELOC-binding sites of pVHL. Patients with causative VHL variants had CNS hemangioblastoma (69.7%), retinal hemangioblastomas (41.4%), clear-cell renal carcinoma (CCRC) (27.3%), renal cysts (22.2%), pancreatic cysts (20.2%), and pheochromocytoma (7.1%). The frequency of multiple pathological changes in targeted organs was significantly higher in patients with causative variants than in the group without mutations, at 78.8% versus 21.1% (p < 0.0001), whereas a single case of CCRC, even in adults under 60 years of age, had a low positive predictive value (14.7%) in relation to P/LP variant detection. The variant c.208G>A;p.Glu70Lys was identified in four patients of East Asian ancestry only; the nonsense variant c.481C>T;p.Arg161* was found significantly more frequently in patients of Turkic ethnicities than in Slavic patients: 30.0 versus 2.5% (p = 0.0047). We did not identify significant differences in the profile of causative germline variants and frequencies of various VHLS clinical manifestations in our cohort compared with other Slavic people. Also, we examined 87 relatives of probands and identified 41 carriers of the causative variants. The obtained results may contribute to improving the diagnosis of VHLS.

papers.title: Curcumin-Based Tyrosinase-Targeting Derivatives for Cell Imaging and Depigmenting Effect.
papers.abstract: Targeting melanogenesis through tyrosinase inhibition represents a key therapeutic strategy, highlighting the need for novel molecules capable of modulating melanin synthesis and/or serving as fluorescent probes for cellular and melanoma tracking. In this study, two curcumin (CUR) derivatives, CUR-C3-PP 1 and CUR-CO-PP 2, were designed and successfully synthesized by strategic integration of a 4-(piperazin-1-yl)phenol pharmacophore into CUR skeleton. In vitro enzymatic assays against Agaricus bisporus tyrosinase (AbTYR) revealed that derivatives CUR-C3-PP 1 and CUR-CO-PP 2 amplified the diphenolase inhibitory capacity (IC50 values of 51.20 μM and 12.89 μM, respectively) when compared to parent curcumin (IC50 = 168.57 μM). Notably, CUR-CO-PP 2 emerged as the most potent candidate, significantly eclipsing native CUR and outperforming the standard inhibitor kojic acid (KA). Enzyme kinetics and molecular docking simulations rationalized this enhanced profile, and the mechanism of inhibitory effects for compounds CUR-C3-PP 1 and CUR-CO-PP 2. Cellular assays highlighted that CUR-C3-PP 1 retained functional intrinsic luminescence, displaying selective accumulation and intense fluorescence within the cytoplasm of B16-F10 melanoma cells alongside preferential cytotoxicity. Screening in zebrafish (Danio rerio) embryos confirmed that both derivatives maintain an excellent biocompatibility profile up to 20 μM. In vivo, both compounds elicited robust, dose-dependent depigmentation, with CUR-CO-PP 2 closely approaching the efficacy of the control 1-phenyl-2-thiourea (PTU). Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the imaging and anti-melanogenic properties of curcuminoids can be independently optimized through rational linker modification, establishing CUR-C3-PP 1 as a promising fluorescent tracer for imaging and CUR-CO-PP 2 as a candidate for depigmenting therapies.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Nanomedicine-Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy in Cutaneous Oncology: Melanoma-Dominant Evidence for Immunogenic Cell Death and Photoimmunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Although photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a recognised treatment for the premalignant keratinocytic lesion actinic keratosis (AK) and selected superficial skin cancers, poor photosensitiser delivery, restricted light penetration and tumour hypoxia can significantly restrict its effectiveness. Recent advances in nanomedicine are extending PDT past improved transport of the photosensitiser. These approaches can also control tumour accumulation, intracellular localisation and the generation of reactive oxygen species. The degree of tumour cell damage is not the only outcome that can be influenced by these features. They can also influence tumour-cell death and immunogenic cell death (ICD)-associated danger signalling and, in selected preclinical systems, support antigen presentation and T-cell activation. Nanomedicine-enhanced PDT has increasingly been integrated with immune-checkpoint blockade and immune adjuvants in melanoma models. In selected preclinical melanoma models, these combinations have improved local tumour control and produced antitumour effects at untreated distant or metastatic sites; functional immune memory has been demonstrated only in a smaller subset of studies using tumour-rechallenge models. Nanotechnology may further address the practical limitations of conventional PDT while improving treatment precision. This is shown by skin-directed delivery, oxygen-generating systems and theranostic platforms. However, immune-related evidence remains predominantly preclinical and melanoma-based, whereas human nanomedicine evidence in AK and basal cell carcinoma (BCC) largely concerns nanoformulation-assisted PDT rather than immune modulation. Overall, the field is progressing from nanoparticle-assisted phototoxicity towards integrated photoimmunotherapy. Treatment delivery, tumour destruction and immune activation are increasingly being considered together. Together, these findings support the continued development of nanomedicine-enhanced PDT across cutaneous oncology, while emphasising that the most advanced immune and photoimmunotherapy evidence currently remains melanoma-based.

papers.title: Advances in Somatostatin Receptor-Targeting Peptide Receptor Radionuclide Therapy for Neuroendocrine Tumors: Biological Rationale, Combination Strategies, and Clinical Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Gastroenteropancreatic (GEP) neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are the most common subtype of NETs, and their incidence continues to increase worldwide. Many NETs express somatostatin receptors (SSTRs), enabling molecular imaging and treatment with radiolabeled somatostatin analogs (SSTAs). [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE is an established treatment for advanced SSTR-positive NETs, but complete and durable responses remain uncommon. This review summarizes current clinical experience with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE and emerging SSTR-targeting radiopharmaceuticals and examines strategies to improve PRRT efficacy. Treatment may be enhanced at several interconnected steps, including increasing receptor availability and tumor targeting, improving radiopharmaceutical uptake and absorbed dose, preventing repair of radiation-induced damage, suppressing cellular stress adaptation and survival, and promoting tumor cell elimination. These approaches include radiation priming and fractionation, somatostatin analog pretreatment, epigenetic modifiers, inhibitors of DNA repair and cellular survival pathways, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy-based combinations. PARP, DNA-PK, and HSP90 inhibitors and chemotherapy-based combinations have shown particularly strong preclinical or clinical evidence, whereas mTOR inhibitors, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, Hedgehog inhibitors, immunotherapy, NAMPT inhibitors, p53 stabilization, and epigenetic modifiers remain under investigation. Ongoing development of novel radiopharmaceuticals, personalized dosimetry, retreatment strategies, and rational combinations is expected to refine PRRT and improve outcomes for patients with NETs.

papers.title: Intercellular Transfer of CD155 Mediated by Melanoma Extracellular Vesicles Downregulates DNAM-1 Expression on NK Cells.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly immunogenic cancer, and immunotherapy is the first-line treatment for patients with advanced disease. However, CD155 overexpression in melanoma has been associated with resistance to immunotherapy. Whether CD155 can be transferred from tumour cells via extracellular vesicles (EVs), and how this transfer affects immune responses in melanoma, remains unclear. To investigate melanoma cell transfer of CD155 in vivo, B16F10-WT and B16F10-CD155KO melanoma cells were subcutaneously injected into CD155-/- mice. We show that CD155 is transferred from melanoma cells to several immune cell populations infiltrating the tumour, at least partly through EV secretion and uptake. DNAM-1 expression was significantly reduced on natural killer (NK) cells in B16F10-WT tumours compared with B16F10-CD155KO tumours. We also found that CD155 was enclosed and enriched in different melanoma EV subtypes. Finally, incubation of NK cells with CD155+ melanoma EVs increased cellular CD155 levels and led to downregulation of DNAM-1. In summary, melanoma-derived CD155 is enriched in melanoma EVs and transferred to immune cells, especially NK cells. Moreover, cancer-derived CD155+ EVs increase CD155 expression on NK cells and are associated with reduced DNAM-1 expression.

papers.title: Somatostatin Receptor Expression and Theranostic Applications Across Non-Neuroendocrine Tumors: A Molecular-to-Clinical Review.
papers.abstract: Somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-targeted imaging and therapy are established approaches for neuroendocrine tumors, but accumulating evidence indicates that SSTRs are also expressed in various non-neuroendocrine tumors. This review aimed to summarize their expression patterns, imaging characteristics, and theranostic potential. Published evidence was reviewed for central nervous system tumors, head and neck cancers, thyroid carcinoma, lung cancer, breast cancer, lymphoma, and melanoma, with particular attention to the cellular localization of SSTR expression and the mechanisms underlying radiotracer uptake. Meningioma, non-keratinizing nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and selected estrogen receptor-positive breast cancers show relatively prominent tumor-cell SSTR expression. In several other malignancies, SSTR expression may predominantly involve tumor-associated macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, or other stromal components. Imaging findings are heterogeneous across and within tumor types. Preliminary studies suggest that peptide receptor radionuclide therapy may provide clinical benefit in selected patients with SSTR-positive non-neuroendocrine tumors, although the available evidence remains limited and largely non-prospective. Further studies integrating quantitative molecular imaging, spatial pathology, and molecular profiling are needed to clarify receptor biology, establish patient-selection criteria, and define the clinical role of SSTR-targeted theranostics beyond neuroendocrine tumors.

papers.title: Peptidoglycan Suppresses Melanoma Growth in a Murine Model with Local Immune Activation.
papers.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes), a Gram-positive cutaneous commensal, has been reported to have antitumor activity in melanoma, but the responsible bacterial components and innate immune pathways remain unclear. Using 8-week-old female C57BL/6NCrSlc mice bearing syngeneic B16-F10 melanoma, we examined heat-killed Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes) and bacterial cell-wall components in an early local co-administration/booster regimen. C. acnes was fractionated into soluble and insoluble components, and peptidoglycan (PG) and lipoteichoic acid (LTA) were evaluated for cytokine induction in splenocytes and CD11b+ myeloid cells in vitro and for tumor control in vivo. Heat-killed C. acnes suppressed melanoma outgrowth, while the insoluble fraction retained TNF-α-inducing and antitumor activity. Both PG and LTA induced TNF-α production in vitro, whereas only PG significantly suppressed melanoma growth in vivo under the tested conditions. PG treatment was associated with extensive tumor necrosis and increased inflammatory cell infiltration. Pharmacologic inhibition of TLR2 or RIPK2 did not fully reverse PG-mediated tumor suppression. Thus, purified Gram-positive PG demonstrated local antitumor immunomodulatory activity and reproduced several features observed with the C. acnes insoluble fraction in this murine melanoma model.

papers.title: PD-L1 in Merkel Cell Carcinoma: From Tumor Microenvironment to Pathological Interpretation.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare, aggressive cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma in which Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) oncoproteins and ultraviolet-induced mutations provide distinct sources of tumor immunogenicity. This narrative review examines the biological determinants, immunohistochemical assessment, and prognostic and therapeutic relevance of programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) in MCC, linking tumor immunobiology to pathological interpretation. PD-L1 expression on tumor and immune cells is often concentrated at tumor-immune interfaces, consistent with interferon-γ-driven adaptive immune resistance. Reported associations with survival and treatment response vary across studies, partly reflecting differences in tissue sampling, assays, scoring compartments, and treatment context. Immune checkpoint blockade can produce durable responses in both PD-L1-positive and PD-L1-negative tumors, while baseline PD-L1 expression alone is not a validated criterion for treatment selection. Resistance mechanisms and emerging biomarkers are discussed alongside viral status, T-cell architecture, antigen-presentation defects, and alternative immune checkpoints. A reporting framework should emphasize specimen characteristics, assay documentation, separate assessment of PD-L1 expression in tumor and immune cells, and spatial heterogeneity. Interpreting PD-L1 within this biological and pathological context supports informative reporting and highlights the potential of integrated spatial biomarkers to improve understanding of immune responsiveness in MCC.

papers.title: The Enemy of My Enemy: Two Cases of De Novo Metastatic Small-Cell Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer with BRCA2 Alterations and Brain Metastases.
papers.abstract: De novo small-cell neuroendocrine prostate cancer (SCNE PC) is a rare and highly aggressive subtype of prostate cancer with limited treatment options. BRCA2 alterations may increase sensitivity to platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibition; however, evidence regarding their clinical relevance in SCNE PC is limited. We present two cases of de novo SCNE PC with distinct BRCA2 alterations. Both patients presented with a similarly extensive disease burden and initially received carboplatin and etoposide (CE), but their clinical courses differed markedly. Patient 1 developed brain metastases three months after completing six cycles of CE and died shortly after rechallenge with CE. In contrast, Patient 2 responded to repeated CE rechallenges, followed by short-term disease control with topotecan and 18 months of disease control with the PARP inhibitor olaparib. He subsequently developed leptomeningeal carcinomatosis and died shortly thereafter, with an overall survival of 5 years and 8 months. These cases illustrate the highly aggressive clinical course of de novo SCNE PC. Despite the potential predictive value of BRCA2 alterations, they may be associated with a higher incidence of brain metastases.

papers.title: Advancing Electrochemotherapy in Melanoma and Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer: From Clinical Practice to Emerging Frontiers.
papers.abstract: Electrochemotherapy (ECT) is a locoregional treatment that combines poorly permeable drugs, commonly bleomycin (BLM) or cisplatin (CDDP), with electric pulses that induce electroporation. By transiently increasing cell membrane permeability, ECT promotes intracellular drug accumulation, enhancing cytotoxic effects while minimizing undesirable systemic toxicity. Beyond its direct cytotoxic effects, ECT exerts additional antitumour mechanisms that contribute to tumour control. These include the induction of immunogenic cell death (ICD), leading to activation of innate and adaptive immune responses; the "abscopal effect", achieved with the combination of ECT and immune checkpoint inhibitors; and the "vascular lock" phenomenon, promoting a transient local blood flow reduction and enhancing intratumoural drug retention; and a "vascular disrupting effect" that contributes to tumour vascular damage and secondary tumour cell death. ECT has demonstrated high objective response rates (ORR) across a wide range of cutaneous malignancies, including melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancers (NMSCs) and cutaneous dissemination of other tumours. Although predictive biomarkers capable of identifying patients who benefit from treatment are still lacking, substantial preclinical and clinical evidence supports the efficacy, safety and tolerability of ECT. Several ongoing clinical trials are currently evaluating ECT, particularly in advanced or non-resecable melanoma, aiming to investigate further biological effects and optimize therapeutic strategies. Furthermore, innovative approaches integrating ECT with gene electrotransfer and nanomedicine represent a promising avenue to enhance its therapeutic efficacy and expand its role in precision oncology.

papers.title: Determination of the Content of Isoquinoline Alkaloids in Selected Plant Extracts and Study of Their Cholinesterase-Inhibiting Activity and Cytotoxicity Against Human Melanoma Cells Using In Vitro and In Silico Methods.
papers.abstract: Different plants containing isoquinoline alkaloids are known to exhibit various biological activities such as anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antiviral, antioxidant, antihyperglycemic, cholesterol-lowering, antifungal and anticancer behaviors. Diseases that pose a significant health burden include neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. Current treatments for these diseases are still inadequate, so new therapeutic agents are needed to treat them more effectively. The aim of this study was to determine the content of selected isoquinoline alkaloids in plant extracts obtained from the leaves of Peumus boldus Molina (Monimi aceae); the rhizomes of Coptis chinensis Franch. (Ranunculaceae); the roots of Jateorhiza palmate (Lam.) Miers (Menispermaceae); the herbs of Eschscholzia californica Cham. (Papaveraceae); and the bark, buds, and flowers of Magnolia officinalis Rehder & E.H.Wilson (Magnoliaceae). The aim of the study was also to determine, in vitro and in silico, the acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitory activity of the investigated isoquinoline alkaloids and the plant extracts containing them. The investigated alkaloid standards and most of the investigated plant extracts exhibited significant anti-cholinesterase activity. Extracts obtained from the rhizomes of Coptis chinensis exhibited the highest activity against acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, with IC50 = 4.85 and 9.58 µg/mL, respectively. The kinetic results indicated that boldine, noncompetitively; coptisine, competitively; and columbamine, in mixed mode, inhibited acetylcholinesterase activity. The activity of butyrylcholinesterase was inhibited by coptisine and columbamine in mixed mode. The next objective of our research was to determine the cytotoxic activity of the tested plant extracts against human melanoma A375 and SK-MEL-3 cell lines. The highest cytotoxicity was observed for the extract obtained from the rhizomes of Coptis chinensis, with IC50 = 4.06 and 27.3 µg/mL against A375 and SK-MEL-3 cells, respectively. All investigated plant extracts exhibited a selectivity index of cytotoxic activity greater than 1.0 against human melanoma cancer cells and fibroblasts, which indicates their selective cytotoxicity towards cancer compared to normal cells. An especially high selectivity index (17.27) was obtained for the Coptis chinensis rhizome extract. Particularly interesting results were obtained for the Coptis chinensis rhizome extract due to its high inhibitory activity against cholinesterases and significant cytotoxicity towards human melanoma cells, combined with a more than seventeen-fold lower toxicity towards fibroblasts; consequently, Coptis chinensis may be particularly recommended for further research.

papers.title: Intratumoral Immunotherapy-The Future of Treating Merkel Cell Carcinoma?
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) represents a rare but highly aggressive neuroendocrine skin cancer with limited systemic therapy options for patients who fail or are ineligible for immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Intratumoral (IT) immunotherapy has emerged as a promising strategy, leveraging the accessibility of tumor lesions and their inherent capacity to trigger immune responses, known as abscopal effects. This review synthesizes the current evidence on IT approaches in MCC, including Toll-like receptor agonists, cytokines, and oncolytic viruses, and highlights their distinct mechanisms of action, while emphasizing the critical need for standardized radiographic response assessment of injected and non-injected lesions. Inconsistent documentation of abscopal responses has hindered quantification of IT therapy's systemic potential, particularly in a disease where one-third of patients present with metastases and distant relapse is common. We outline MCC-specific rationale for routine lesion-level tracking, and recommendations for IT trial designs and objectives. Rigorous assessments of abscopal data will clarify IT's role as both rescue therapy and an ICI partner, potentially transforming outcomes in this refractory MCC.

papers.title: Same-Day Coordination of Mohs Surgery, Lymphoscintigraphy, and Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy for Merkel Cell Carcinoma: A Single-Center Feasibility Report.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is an aggressive neuroendocrine tumor, most commonly occurring on the head and neck. Incidence of MCC is rising with the aging population. Five-year overall survival (OS) for localized MCC is 50.6%; 5-year OS for patients with distant metastases is 13.5%. The purpose of this study is to determine if coordination of care for the treatment of MCC is logistically feasible, and provide a description of the patient population observed at this institution. Methods: All patients with MCC diagnosis from January 2012-June 2024 were identified at our tertiary care center. All patients with MCC were added to our non-melanoma skin cancer registry. Outcomes were compared between those treated with our "Merkel cell carcinoma in a day" (MIAD) protocol and those receiving the standard treatment protocol. Results: No significant differences were detected in the recurrence rate, transit metastasis, distant metastasis, and disease-specific death. Nodal metastasis was higher in the MIAD group (HR 4.94, 95% CI 1.08-22.6, p = 0.039, six events total). Both groups had similar times to treatment and treatment within 30 days of diagnosis. Conclusions: MCC is a rare and aggressive tumor, often exhibiting subclinical tumor spread. Mohs micrographic surgery ensures 100% peripheral and deep margin assessment, with potential for tissue sparing. With thoughtful coordination, lymphoscintigraphy can be completed on the same day as Mohs surgery followed by sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) and reconstructive surgery.

papers.title: Treatment Sequencing in ARPI-Pre-Exposed Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Radioligand Therapy, PARP Inhibitors, and Antibody-Drug Conjugates.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) intensification in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer has changed the population reaching metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), and the optimal sequence of subsequent therapies is uncertain. Methods: The study presents a narrative review of phase II/III trials reporting radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) or overall survival (OS) in mCRPC, including congress data, to June 2026, graded on a five-level evidence hierarchy. Results: No prospective sequencing trial has been reported. CARD (cabazitaxel versus an ARPI switch after docetaxel; OS HR 0.64) remains the clearest sequencing dataset. Alpha-controlled OS benefit for PARP inhibitors is established in the PROfound cohort A (HR 0.69) and in the TALAPRO-2 all-comer population (HR 0.80); larger BRCA-specific estimates are exploratory, and BRCA OS in TRITON3 was not improved (HR 0.91). 177Lu-PSMA-617 improved rPFS versus an ARPI switch in PSMAfore, but intention-to-treat OS did not differ (HR 0.91) amid 60% crossover; no taxane-controlled trial has shown an OS advantage, and in preliminary PLUDO data, OS favoured docetaxel first (HR 1.64), a difference potentially confounded by asymmetric crossover. Conclusions: We propose a hypothesis-generating four-track framework stratified by homologous recombination repair status and PSMA-PET expression; treatment choice remains individualised.

papers.title: Toward Precision Imaging in Lung NET: A Clinically Oriented Framework Integrating Dual Tracer PET and Radiomics.
papers.abstract: Background: Pulmonary neuroendocrine tumors (lung NETs) comprise a biologically heterogeneous group of neoplasms ranging from indolent typical carcinoids to more aggressive atypical carcinoids. Accurate characterization of tumor biology is essential for optimizing staging, prognostic stratification, and treatment selection. Beyond conventional cross-sectional imaging, functional imaging and emerging quantitative imaging techniques are progressively redefining the diagnostic pathway. Methods: We performed a comprehensive narrative review of the current evidence regarding conventional radiological imaging, somatostatin receptor (SSTR) PET/CT, 18F-FDG PET/CT, dual-tracer imaging, and radiomics in lung NETs, integrating recent international recommendations from ENETS, ESMO, AIOM, and other major societies. Results: Contrast-enhanced CT remains the cornerstone of anatomical staging, whereas 68Ga-labelled somatostatin analogue (SSA) PET/CT provides highly sensitive assessment of receptor expression and patient eligibility for somatostatin analogue therapy and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). Conversely, 18F-FDG PET/CT identifies metabolically active and biologically aggressive disease, particularly in atypical carcinoids and tumors showing dedifferentiation. Increasing evidence supports the complementary role of dual-tracer PET/CT for non-invasive characterization of tumor heterogeneity, prognostic stratification, and treatment planning. Radiomics further expands this paradigm by extracting quantitative imaging biomarkers that may improve histological prediction, recurrence risk assessment, and individualized management. Although promising, radiomics remains limited by methodological heterogeneity and the lack of prospective validation. Conclusions: The integration of conventional imaging, molecular imaging, and quantitative radiomics supports a shift from lesion detection toward biologically driven precision imaging. Future prospective multicenter studies incorporating imaging biomarkers, artificial intelligence, and clinical-pathological variables may further support personalized management of patients with lung NETs.

papers.title: Redox Storm in the Tumor Microenvironment (ΤΜΕ): Multifaceted Redox Injury and Immunometabolic Reprogramming Induced by Immune Checkpoint Blockade in B16F10 Melanoma: An Ultrastructural Study of the Peritumoral Interface.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized melanoma treatment, yet the in vivo ultrastructural consequences within the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain poorly characterized. This study investigates the morphological alterations induced by ICB at the peritumoral interface through a "redox storm" paradigm. B16F10 melanoma-bearing mice were treated with anti-CTLA-4, anti-PD-1, or their combination, and evaluated by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) at Days 20, 30, and 40; quantitative morphometric analyses were performed for comparative purposes. This design enabled the assessment of ultrastructural changes from initial immune activation to late-stage remodeling, linking early cytotoxic events with subsequent stromal adaptations. TEM provided evidence of a sequential redox cascade characterized by lymphocyte reactivation, mitochondrial cristolysis, lipid droplet accumulation, foamy macrophage-like cells, efferocytosis-driven M2-like polarization, and metabolic plasticity in surviving tumor cells. Specifically, combination therapy was associated with marked cytolysis and extensive stromal remodeling, while anti-PD-1 appeared to promote prominent cholesterol crystal formation and lipotoxicity. Morphometric analyses supported these qualitative findings, indicating significant alterations in lipid droplet area and cell death area across treatment groups. This ultrastructural dissection provides morphological evidence for the "redox storm" and offers a framework to understand ICB efficacy, resistance, and dynamic TME remodeling, ultimately providing a basis for targeted combination strategies.

papers.title: Advanced Carcinoid Tricuspid Valve Disease Associated with Delayed Recognition and Loss of the Interventional Window in a Patient with Ileal Neuroendocrine Tumor: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Carcinoid heart disease remains one of the most serious complications of carcinoid syndrome, yet cardiac involvement may still be recognized late, when valvular damage is already advanced and treatment options are limited. Case Presentation: We report a 70-year-old man with a well-differentiated ileal neuroendocrine tumor (NET G2, Ki-67 up to 5%), diagnosed in December 2019. Over six years, the disease progressed with liver metastases, markedly rising 24 h urinary 5-HIAA levels and clinically active carcinoid syndrome, and was treated sequentially with somatostatin analogues, everolimus and 177Lu-DOTATOC. Throughout this period, oncological evaluation was frequent, whereas structured cardiac assessment was essentially absent until 2025. When the patient was referred for evaluation for transcatheter tricuspid repair, echocardiography demonstrated advanced carcinoid tricuspid valve disease with severe regurgitation, mild stenosis, marked leaflet thickening and tethering, and a coaptation gap of 17 mm-far beyond the ~7 mm threshold associated with favorable edge-to-edge repair and the >10 mm range associated with poor outcome. Because of the advanced valve remodeling and the overall clinical burden, the patient was not a candidate for transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or surgery and subsequently died. Conclusions: This case illustrates how carcinoid heart disease can progress beyond correctability and supports regular echocardiographic surveillance in patients with carcinoid syndrome, so that valve involvement is identified while intervention is still anatomically feasible.

papers.title: Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs) of the Larynx.
papers.abstract: To review the current state of knowledge regarding neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) of the larynx, with a particular focus on their epidemiology, etiopathogenesis, clinico-pathological features, immunohistochemical profile, and differential diagnostics. Narrative review. Diagnostic criteria for laryngeal NETs were recently defined in the 5th edition of the WHO Classification of Head and Neck Tumors, which newly introduces the entity of NET, grade 3 (G3 NET). However, some of these criteria are still considered provisional. The most common NET of the larynx is the G2 NET. These tumors typically affect older men, with the supraglottic region being the most frequent localization. For a definitive diagnosis, it is essential to demonstrate the epithelial origin and neuroendocrine differentiation of these tumors using cytokeratins and neuroendocrine markers (e.g., chromogranin, INSM1, synaptophysin). The differentiation between individual NET types is based on mitotic activity and/or Ki-67 proliferation index, as well as the presence or absence of necrosis. Laryngeal NETs typically exhibit wild-type p53 expression and retained Rb1 and somatostatin receptor 2 expression. This can be utilized in the differential diagnosis from neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs). Given that laryngeal NETs frequently express calcitonin, they must be differentiated from medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), particularly in lymph node metastases. A high frequency of HRAS gene mutations has been recently demonstrated in laryngeal NETs, underlining their distinctness from their gastroenteropancreatic and thoracopulmonary counterparts. By utilizing the proposed diagnostic criteria for individual types of laryngeal NETs, it is anticipated that more precise knowledge regarding the clinico-pathological characteristics of these exceedingly rare tumors will be obtained, particularly with respect to their biological behavior and prognosis.

papers.title: Multidisciplinary Management of Neuroendocrine Neoplasms Beyond Centers of Excellence: Retrospective Real-World Data from a Referral Center in Eastern Europe.
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) require multidisciplinary management, yet access to advanced imaging and therapies is uneven across Europe. We aimed to describe real-world management of NENs in an Eastern Europe referral center. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 192 NEN patients treated between 2011 and 2026 at a national referral center in Romania. Results: Most tumors were well-differentiated (88%), pancreatic primary (59.9%), and non-functioning (77.1%); 51.0% were metastatic at diagnosis. Overall, 30.7% (n = 59) of patients underwent somatostatin receptor imaging, mainly with locally available 99mTc-HYNIC-TOC scintigraphy (n = 56). Among therapeutic modalities, 68.2% of patients underwent conventional systemic therapy and 69.3% had surgery (R0 resection was achieved in 98.9% of curative-intent surgeries; recurrence rate 40%). Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) was performed in 14.6% (19/130) of metastatic NENs and liver-directed therapy (LDT) in 13.6% (16/118) of NENs with liver metastases. Median time to treatment was 78 days for somatostatin analogs, 29 days for chemotherapy in neuroendocrine carcinoma, 30 days for surgery, 62.5 days for LDT, and 144 days for PRRT. Conclusions: This is one of the few reports on real-world management of NENs in an Eastern European tertiary care referral center, which highlights the available multidisciplinary care but also the challenges in diagnostics and therapeutic access for patients with NEN.

Feasibility of Laparoscopic Partial Cystectomy for Bladder Paraganglioma: A Four-Case Series.
papers.abstract: Urinary bladder paraganglioma is a rare tumor associated with a risk of catecholamine-induced hypertensive crisis during tumor manipulation. The optimal surgical approach remains uncertain, particularly for larger tumors or those with suspected local invasion. We report four cases managed at our institution. All tumors were diagnosed preoperatively by magnetic resonance imaging and 123I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scintigraphy, and all patients received preoperative α-blockade. Three tumors (1.0-1.5 cm) without extravesical extension were treated with laparoscopic partial cystectomy without conversion. One larger tumor (4.3 cm) with suspected local invasion was managed using a planned open procedure and was associated with marked intraoperative hypertension and technical difficulty. These findings suggest that laparoscopic partial cystectomy is technically feasible in selected patients with small, localized bladder paragangliomas, whereas tumor size and suspected local invasion may influence surgical planning. The technical requirements for complete resection and catecholamine-related hemodynamic risk should be assessed separately.

papers.title: Locally Advanced Disease and Clinical Outcomes of Pheochromocytomas and Paragangliomas: Insights from a Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the prognostic significance of locally advanced disease (LAD) in patients with pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs). We retrospectively analyzed 389 patients with histopathologically confirmed PPGLs from 19 tertiary centers. LAD was defined as capsular, periadrenal fat, adjacent-organ, or vascular invasion. Persistent/recurrent disease was the composite primary endpoint. The prognostic value of LAD was further assessed after excluding patients with distant metastatic disease at diagnosis, in patients with stage I-II disease, and in combination with Ki-67 labeling index (LI) ≥3%. LAD was identified in 111 patients (28.5%). Persistent/recurrent disease occurred in 17.1% and 6.1% of patients with and without LAD, respectively (p<0.001), with corresponding 5-year disease-free survival (DFS) rates of 81.8% and 93.4% (log-rank p<0.001). LAD remained independently associated with persistent/recurrent disease in multivariable analysis (HR, 3.64; 95% CI, 1.55-8.52; p=0.003). Its prognostic association persisted after excluding patients with distant metastatic disease at diagnosis. Among patients with stage I-II disease, 5-year DFS was 84.8% and 95.5% with and without LAD, respectively (log-rank p=0.014), and adding LAD to the TNM-only model significantly improved model fit (likelihood-ratio p=0.025). Patients with both LAD and Ki-67 LI ≥3% had a 5-year DFS of 68.5%. LAD was associated with unfavorable outcomes in PPGLs and provided additional prognostic information beyond TNM stage in stage I-II disease. Combined assessment of local invasiveness and proliferative activity warrants further evaluation for risk stratification.

papers.title: A telomere-to-telomere map of somatic mutation burden and functional impact in a cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer genomes harbor extensive somatic genetic and epigenetic variation, yet large portions of the genome remain inaccessible to conventional reference-based analyses. Here, we demonstrate that pairing a near-telomere-to-telomere (near-T2T) diploid assembly of a donor with deep short- and long-read sequencing of their melanoma reveals that 16% of somatic variants localize to sequences absent from GRCh38, with satellite repeats acting as hotspots for UV-associated mutagenesis. Centromere kinetochore binding domains emerge as focal sites of chromosome arm aneuploidy breakpoints and somatic genetic variation, features we further demonstrate are also present in non-cancerous tissues. By contrast, extensive epigenetic remodeling of kinetochore binding domains appears specific to oncogenesis. Single-molecule telomere analyses reconstruct the cycle of telomere erosion and telomerase-mediated extension during tumor evolution, while haplotype-resolved chromatin maps reveal widespread somatic epimutations impacting regulatory elements. Together, these findings define previously inaccessible dimensions of somatic variation and establish a framework for telomere-to-telomere studies of human mosaicism.

papers.title: Interpretable CT-based radiomics nomogram integrating clinical and semantic features for preoperative grading of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms: a shap-based analysis.
papers.abstract: Preoperative grading of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PNENs) is crucial for personalized management. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning framework based on CT imaging to predict PNENs pathological grades. We retrospectively analyzed 125 patients with pathologically confirmed PNENs, divided into training and test cohorts. A comprehensive radiomics pipeline was implemented, involving the extraction of high-dimensional features from CT images. We constructed three predictive models: a clinical model, a radiomics model, and a fusion model. To ensure methodological robustness, seven machine-learning algorithms were employed and cross-validated to identify the optimal classifier. Furthermore, the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) method was utilized to decode the "black box" of the radiomics signature. The fusion model-integrating CT radiomic signatures with semantic hallmarks-consistently outperformed the standalone clinical and radiomics models, achieving a superior AUC of 0.891 in the validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that microscopic texture complexity (e.g., Zone Entropy) and macro-geometric irregularity (e.g., Sphericity) were the dominant predictors, aligning with the biological aggressiveness of high-grade lesions. By integrating multi-dimensional CT features with a rigorous machine-learning consensus, our study provides a highly accurate and interpretable "virtual biopsy" tool.

papers.title: Immunomodulatory actions of catecholamines, cluster-specific signaling pathways, and metabolites in pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms with an exceptionally high genetic contribution, often driven by single high-penetrance mutations. Approximately one third of patients harbor germline mutations and another third carry somatic driver mutations, allowing stratification into three molecular clusters: pseudohypoxia-related (cluster 1), kinase signaling-related (cluster 2) and Wnt-signaling-related (cluster 3). These clusters differ in catecholamine secretion, malignancy, and metastatic behavior. Although PPGLs have long been viewed as immunologically 'cold' due to their low neoantigen load and limited T cell infiltration, recent studies show a more complex immune landscape, with differences observed between indolent and metastatic tumors, and between genomic clusters. The interaction between the tumor and immune system is, in general, closely associated with tumorigenesis and disease prognosis, with both the innate and adaptive immune system playing pivotal roles. This review summarizes how tumor-derived catecholamines and cluster-specific genetic drivers and metabolic programs are able to orchestrate immune modulation in PPGL. Within clusters of PPGL, distinct metabolic and signaling alterations such as pseudohypoxia, tricarboxylic acid cycle oncometabolites, and aberrant kinase and B-catenin signaling shape both the tumor microenvironment and systemic immune response. We highlight therapeutic opportunities together with approaches that harness or reprogram innate immune memory. Recognizing PPGL as metabolically and immunologically stratified tumors may enable rational, personalized combination therapies for patients with inoperable, recurrent or metastatic disease, and might explain the heterogeneous response to immunotherapy currently observed.

papers.title: Immunohistochemical Analysis of INSM1, MCPyV, and PHOX2B Expression in Merkel Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and aggressive cutaneous neuroendocrine malignancy with distinct etiological pathways, including Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) infection and ultraviolet (UV)-induced carcinogenesis. Owing to the lack of large case series, the etiology of MCC in Turkey remains unclear. INSM1 is a highly specific neuroendocrine marker that supports the diagnosis of MCC. PHOX2B, although known to be expressed in neuroblastoma, has been only rarely investigated in MCC. We retrospectively evaluated 14 MCC cases diagnosed between 2008 and 2023 at Istanbul Training and Research Hospital. Immunohistochemical analysis was performed using antibodies against INSM1 (A-8), MCPyV (Ab3), and PHOX2B (EP312). The extent and pattern of staining were assessed and correlated with clinicopathological findings and existing literature. All cases demonstrated INSM1 expression, with predominantly diffuse nuclear staining. MCPyV positivity was observed in 78.6% of cases. PHOX2B expression was detected in only one case, showing focal and weak nuclear positivity, while all other cases were negative. Our findings support the high diagnostic utility of INSM1 and confirm that MCPyV is present in most MCC cases in our cohort. The use of the Ab3 antibody may enhance detection of MCPyV due to its higher sensitivity. Since neuroblastoma and Merkel cell carcinoma are morphologically similar on first glance with sheets of small blue cells, PHOX2B serves as an effective discriminatory marker. It tests positive in neuroblastoma and negative in Merkel cell carcinoma, as demonstrated in our cohort of patients. These findings highlight the importance of appropriate marker selection in the diagnostic evaluation of MCC. Merkel cell carcinomas secondary to viral etiology appear to be the predominant form in Turkey.

papers.title: Predictors of Visual Outcomes in Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor Resection.
papers.abstract: We sought to identify clinical and radiologic predictors of visual recovery and explore visual outcomes in patients who underwent transsphenoidal resection of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). Retrospective study of patients with PitNETs approaching/contacting the chiasm at a tertiary neuro-ophthalmology practice. Clinical/demographic/MRI data were analyzed. Patients with a final visual acuity (VA) of at least 20/40 and a final visual field mean deviation (VF MD) of -5 dB or better were defined as positive outcomes. 68 patients were analyzed, including 44 patients who underwent surgery and 24 who were observed during the study period. Of those who underwent surgery, patients with positive VA outcomes had better preoperative VA (logMAR 0.3 vs 1.3), VF MD (-8.1 vs -17.9 dB), thicker retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) (81.9 vs 69.5 µm) and ganglion cell complexes (GCC) (69.0 vs 50.5 µm) than those without. VF outcomes were predicted by better preoperative VA (logMAR 0.3 vs 0.7), VF MD (-7.4 vs -14.5 dB), thicker RNFL (84.1 vs 70.5 µm) and GCC (71.2 vs 55.6 µm) measurements and smaller tumor volume (8.4 vs 18.2 cm3). Preoperative VA/VF MD/RNFL/GCC thickness may predict visual outcomes after PitNET resection. Neuroradiologic factors failed to predict visual outcomes.
