papers.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

papers.title: Recurrent Intermittent Small Bowel Obstruction as an Initial Manifestation of Primary Intestinal Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Case Report and Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Primary intestinal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a rare gastrointestinal malignancy and an uncommon cause of small bowel obstruction (SBO). We report a 70-year-old man with no history of abdominal surgery who presented with recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, vomiting, and transiently resolving SBO. Serial computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a persistent transition point associated with an increasingly evident mesenteric soft tissue mass, initially suspected to represent a neuroendocrine tumor. After repeated presentations and temporary improvement with conservative management, exploratory laparotomy revealed a distal ileal tumor with central mesenteric involvement encasing major mesenteric vessels. Segmental small bowel resection with primary anastomosis was performed, although macroscopic mesenteric disease remained. Histopathological examination confirmed CD10-positive DLBCL, and systemic treatment with six cycles of R-CHOP was initiated. A structured search of MEDLINE and Embase identified 78 publications describing 87 adult cases of intestinal lymphoma presenting with SBO. DLBCL was the most frequently reported subtype, and the ileum was the most commonly specified anatomical location. However, recurrent obstruction with transient clinical and radiological improvement was rarely emphasized. This case demonstrates that temporary resolution of obstructive symptoms does not exclude a persistent pathological lead point. Recurrent SBO in a patient without previous abdominal surgery, particularly when serial imaging demonstrates evolving mesenteric or intestinal abnormalities, should prompt renewed investigation for an underlying malignancy, including intestinal lymphoma. Repeat cross-sectional imaging, multidisciplinary reassessment, and individualized consideration of operative exploration may facilitate timely diagnosis while avoiding conclusions that transient improvement represents definitive resolution.

papers.title: Dual-targeting theranostic strategies to overcome receptor heterogeneity in neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PC) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy characterized by dynamic alterations in surface biomarker expression during disease progression. Although prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) remains the most clinically established target for PC imaging and therapy, receptor heterogeneity remains a major obstacle in advanced, treatment-resistant, and neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC). These limitations have driven increasing interest in dual-targeting strategies to improve tumor coverage and therapeutic precision. Neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) is predominantly expressed in aggressive androgen-independent and neuroendocrine tumors, whereas gastrin-releasing peptide receptor (GRPR) is highly expressed in early-stage and low-Gleason-score prostate cancer. The complementary expression profiles of PSMA, GRPR, and NTSR1 provide a strong rationale for developing dual-targeted theranostic platforms capable of overcoming tumor heterogeneity and lineage plasticity of advanced PC. This review discusses the biological significance, signaling pathways, expression dynamics, and recent advances in dual-targeting strategies for imaging and therapy of advanced PC.

papers.title: Management of Merkel Cell Carcinoma of the Digits, Hand, and Wrist.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and often lethal cancer, with few cases presenting on the hand and digits. Treatments such as ray amputation can drastically impact quality of life and the existing literature is inconclusive. This systematic review evaluates the comprehensive management of surgically treated patients with MCC involving the digits, hand, and wrist. Following PRISMA guidelines, Medline and EMBASE were searched for studies reporting MCC of the digits, hand, and wrist. Given the heterogeneity of the reported data, no meta-analysis was performed; results are reported descriptively as counts/proportions among cases with available data. Forty-two observational studies were included. Twenty-two reported MCC of the digit (25 lesions), of which 15/25 (60%) underwent wide local excision (WLE) and 10/25 (40%) ray amputation. Among cases with available data, recurrence occurred in 2/7 (29%) after WLE and 2/8 (25%) after ray amputation, with MCC-related mortality in 2/9 (22%) of each. Nineteen studies reported MCC of the hand/wrist (n = 19), of which 17/19 (89%) underwent WLE, with recurrence in 7/14 (50%) and MCC-related mortality in 2/12 (17%). Adjuvant radiotherapy and chemotherapy were used in 10/19 (53%) and 4/19 (21%), and nodal management included sentinel lymph node biopsy in 5/13 (38%) and dissection in 4/13 (31%). An additional aggregate cohort of 25 patients was summarized separately. Evidence for MCC of the digits, hand and wrist is limited to case reports and small series with heterogeneous staging/treatment and incomplete reporting. Further evidence is needed to determine optimal management in this region.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of bevacizumab plus XELOX in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are highly vascularized malignancies for which effective treatment options remain limited in the unresectable locally advanced or metastatic setting. Although platinum-based chemotherapy has demonstrated antitumor activity in advanced NETs, evidence supporting its combination with antiangiogenic therapy remains insufficient. In this retrospective study, 85 patients with progressive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic well-differentiated NETs initiated bevacizumab plus XELOX, consisting of bevacizumab at 7.5 mg/kg and oxaliplatin at 130 mg/m² every 3 weeks, together with capecitabine at 1,000 mg/m² twice daily on days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle. Among them, 72 patients who completed at least two treatment cycles and underwent post-baseline radiological evaluations comprised the safety set. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) by RECIST v1.1, while secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Among the efficacy-evaluable patients, 62 (86.1%) received the regimen as second-line or later systemic therapy. Best responses included complete response (CR) in 1 patient (1.4%), partial response (PR) in 29 (40.3%), stable disease (SD) in 41 (56.9%), and progressive disease (PD) in 1 (1.4%), resulting in an ORR of 41.7% and a DCR of 98.6%. In a conservative sensitivity analysis encompassing all 85 treated patients-treating the 13 non-evaluable patients as non-responders-the ORR was 35.3%. After a median follow-up of 17.2 months, the median PFS was 20.9 months (95% CI, 13.7 months-not reached), with 6-, 12-, and 24-month PFS rates of 84.7%, 69.6%, and 47.3%, respectively. Median OS was not reached, and OS data remained immature. The most frequent any-grade adverse events (AEs) were elevated aspartate aminotransferase (48.6%), anemia (44.4%), lymphopenia and hypoalbuminemia (41.7% each), and hyperglycemia (40.3%), while neutropenia was the most frequent individual grade ≥3 AE (5.6%). No grade ≥3 bevacizumab-specific toxicities were observed. These findings suggest that bevacizumab plus XELOX demonstrates clinically meaningful antitumor activity and a manageable safety profile in advanced NET patients. Given the retrospective and single-arm design, this regimen may represent a potential alternative or sequential treatment option when alkylating-agent-based chemotherapy is unsuitable, whereas prospective comparative studies are warranted to validate these findings and determine its optimal clinical role.

papers.title: Clinicopathological Features of DLL3 Expression and T-Cell Infiltration in LCNEC: Insights From Pathology and Clinical Response to Tarlatamab.
papers.abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare and aggressive lung neuroendocrine neoplasm with poor prognosis. Recently, DLL3-targeted bispecific T-cell engagers (BiTEs) have shown promising efficacy in small cell lung cancer, and clinical trials are ongoing in LCNEC. This study evaluated DLL3 expression and CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) infiltration in LCNEC and investigated their clinical significance and association with tarlatamab efficacy. We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients who were diagnosed with LCNEC. Immunohistochemical analyses for DLL3 and CD8 were performed. DLL3 positivity was defined as staining in ≥ 1% of tumor cells. CD8+ TIL infiltration was graded as low, moderate, or high. Among 77 screened LCNEC cases, 44 were eligible for analysis. The median age was 75 years. DLL3 expression was observed in 70.5% of cases and was associated with worse survival. Low CD8+ TIL infiltration was observed in 59.1% of cases. Patients with high CD8+ TIL infiltration demonstrated significantly longer survival than those with low infiltration (p = 0.03). Among representative clinical cases, a patient with DLL3 (+)/CD8 TILs (-) LCNEC achieved marked tumor shrinkage, whereas a patient with DLL3 (-)/CD8 TILs (-) LCNEC showed no response. DLL3 is frequently expressed in LCNEC and correlates with a poorer prognosis. A majority of LCNEC cases are immunologically characterized as cold tumors lacking CD8+ TILs, which contributes to unfavorable clinical outcomes. Tarlatamab induced a robust antitumor response even in a DLL3 (+) cold tumor. DLL3-BiTE represents a promising therapeutic strategy for DLL3 (+) LCNEC.

papers.title: Histopathologic features and subtypes of invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: A comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: Invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is the second most common cutaneous malignancy after basal cell carcinoma and displays a remarkably heterogeneous spectrum of histopathologic variants, several of which pose significant diagnostic challenges and carry distinct clinical, immunohisto-chemical, and molecular implications. In this review, we discuss the principal histopathologic subtypes of invasive cSCC, including acantholytic, sarcomatoid (carcinosarcoma/metaplastic), spindle cell, clear cell, verrucous, papillary, pigmented, adenosquamous, signet ring cell, rhabdoid, lymphoepithelial, and squamo-melanocytic variants, as well as cSCC associated with Merkel cell carcinoma and tumors showing single-cell infiltration. For each entity, we summarize the characteristic clinical presentation, key histopathological features, differential diagnosis, immunohistochemical profile, and, where available, molecular alterations, with particular attention to UV-induced mutations in TP53, NOTCH1/2, and CDKN2A shared across most subtypes. Treatment and prognostic data are also reviewed, highlighting that while most variants follow conventional surgical principles for cSCC, with margin-controlled excision and Mohs micrographic surgery playing a central role, certain subtypes-namely spindle cell/sarcomatoid, rhabdoid, and tumors with single-cell infiltration-are associated with markedly more aggressive behavior and require intensified management. Conversely, entities such as acantholytic, clear cell, verrucous, papillary, and pigmented SCC generally behave indolently despite sometimes alarming histological appearances. Overall, prognosis in cSCC remains primarily driven by established risk factors-tumor size, depth, differentiation, location, and perineural invasion-rather than histologic subtype alone. A refined understanding of these variants, supported by targeted immunohistochemistry and molecular evaluation when indicated, is essential for accurate diagnosis, appropriate risk stratification, and optimal treatment planning.

papers.title: Spatial and Single-Cell Multi-Omics Analyses of T-Cell Subsets and Interactions in Melanoma Lymph Node Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly immunogenic malignancy, yet responses to systemic therapy remain variable. The tumour-draining lymph node (TDLN), including the sentinel lymph node (SLN) during early regional spread, is not only a site of metastatic dissemination but also an important setting for T-cell priming and immune regulation. Conventional classification of nodes as tumour-positive or tumour-negative provides essential staging information but reveals little about their immune state. Single-cell immune transcriptomics, T-cell receptor sequencing and single-cell epigenomics now allow T-cell states, clonal dynamics and regulatory programmes to be examined in greater detail. Spatial transcriptomics, multiplex imaging, spatial proteomics and emerging spatial metabolomics add the anatomical context needed to determine where these cells and molecular programmes occur within the intact tissue architecture. In this review, we examine how these approaches are being utilised to study T-cell heterogeneity, spatial organisation and immune interactions within melanoma TDLNs, together with the emerging contribution of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted pathology. We also critically evaluate how these technologies are applied, with attention to tissue requirements, spatial resolution, molecular coverage, computational demands, scalability to archival haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) imaging cohorts and careful interpretation of predicted or inferred spatial features. By combining biological profiling with methodological appraisal, we highlight how multi-omics immune signatures may refine nodal disease assessment and guide future biomarker development, while noting that clinical translation will require standardised analytical pipelines and disease-specific validation across independent melanoma cohorts.

papers.title: Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Ethanol Ablation for Benign Insulinoma: A Single-Centre Experience and Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Insulinoma is a predominantly benign pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour that is traditionally managed surgically. However, surgical invasiveness and anaesthesia-related risks limit its applicability in selected patients. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided ethanol ablation has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and feasibility of EUS-guided ethanol ablation for benign insulinoma. We retrospectively analysed 17 patients with insulinoma who underwent EUS-guided ethanol ablation, predominantly as a primary treatment. All procedures were performed by experienced gastroenterologists using 95% absolute ethanol. The study cohort had a mean age of 58.47 ± 12.29 years and a mean disease duration of 34.43 months (range, 0.36-84.0). Clinical success was achieved in 16 patients (94.1%). One patient with an initial suboptimal response successfully underwent a repeat ablation after 8 months. Over a median follow-up period of 46.1 months (range, 6.6-97.8), one patient was lost to follow-up. Disease recurrence was observed in four patients, resulting in a recurrence rate of 25% (4/16) among those with available follow-up data. Three recurrent cases underwent repeat ablation, all achieving symptomatic resolution. A total of 22 ablation procedures were performed. Adverse events were documented in 36.4% (8/22) of procedures, with the majority being mild (31.8%, 7/22) and one severe adverse event (4.5%, 1/22). EUS-guided ethanol ablation is an effective and well-tolerated treatment for benign insulinoma. It represents a viable minimally invasive alternative to surgery and remains effective for managing recurrence or initial treatment failure without compromising subsequent surgical options.

papers.title: Decoupling T cell cytotoxicity: a CCL21+ICAM1-based synthetic immune niche enhances tumor elimination by accelerating lytic hit delivery.
papers.abstract: Preserving T cell cytotoxic function during ex vivo expansion remains a major challenge for adoptive cancer immunotherapy. A synthetic immune niche (SIN) composed of immobilized CCL21 and ICAM1 was shown to improve T cell expansion while preserving cytotoxicity; however, it remains unclear which specific step of the T cell killing process is enhanced by the SIN stimulation. Here, we combined advanced imaging based on time-lapse microscopy with a mean-field model to analyze the distinct stages in killing of B16 melanoma cells by CD8[Formula: see text] T cells. This framework enabled us to resolve the tumor cell killing process into discrete steps throughout target cell engagement with SIN-treated T cells and lytic hit delivery. We found that tumor cell death is best explained by a multi-hit process, requiring approximately four discrete hits to trigger cell death. Model-based analysis identified a significant increase in the lytic hit-delivery rate, [Formula: see text], as the main kinetic change associated with the enhanced cytotoxicity of SIN-treated T cells. The target encounter rate, [Formula: see text], could not be reliably compared between conditions because it was practically non-identifiable in the untreated dataset. Global sensitivity analysis further showed that increasing lytic hit delivery has a stronger effect on tumour control than increasing target encounter rates. These findings fundamentally reorient our understanding of optimized T cell manufacturing, suggesting that the lytic execution step may be the primary rate-limiting bottleneck in this in-vitro system, and that engineering strategies targeting granule polarization or discharge warrant prioritization alongside affinity-enhancement approaches.

papers.title: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms: A 20-year experience at a tertiary care medical center in Mexico City.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms are a heterogeneous group of tumors, primarily located in the gastroenteropancreatic system. In Mexico, clinical and epidemiologic data on them are limited. Our aim was to describe the experience with gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms at a tertiary care medical center and analyze the factors associated with survival. A retrospective analytic cohort study was conducted. The study included 110 patients with a mean age of 58 years (SD ± 13.8), 55.5% of whom were women. The pancreas was the most common primary site (50%). Functional tumors accounted for 28.2% of cases and carcinoid syndrome for 9.1%. Performance status was preserved in 96.3% of patients (ECOG 0-1). At diagnosis, 50% presented with advanced disease, of whom 61.3% had high hepatic tumor burden. The median follow-up period was 37.5 months. Overall survival (OS) was 162 months (SD ± 12.8). The factors associated with better OS were preserved performance status (p < 0.001), CgA ≤ 700 ng/mL (p = 0.02), Ki-67 < 5% (p = 0.03), and low hepatic tumor burden (p = 0.02). The factors associated with better progression-free survival were preserved performance status (p = 0.022), histologic grade (p = 0.02), CgA ≤ 700 ng/mL (p = 0.03), and objective response rate (p < 0.001). At our medical center, the most frequent primary site was the pancreas and most of the patients were women, differing from international reports. Factors associated with better survival were identified, including preserved performance status, CgA ≤ 700 ng/mL, histologic grade, Ki-67 < 5%, low hepatic tumor burden, and objective response rate.

papers.title: Adamantinoma-like Ewing Sarcoma: An Underrecognized Mimicker in the Head and Neck With Divergent Clinicopathologic Features from Ewing Sarcoma.
papers.abstract: Adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma (ALES) is a cytokeratin-positive member of the Ewing sarcoma (ES) family with a predilection for the head and neck (HN). Its rarity and overlapping immunophenotype with carcinomas contribute to frequent misclassification, while its biologic behavior and response to standard ES therapy remain incompletely defined. We conducted a 25-year retrospective review to characterize the clinicopathologic spectrum of ALES and compare HN ALES with non-HN ALES and HN ES, incorporating histologic, immunophenotypic, molecular, and clinical outcome data. Twenty-three cases were identified; ALES (n=20) and HN ES (n=3). ALES occurred in older patients (median age 49 vs. 29 years) and demonstrated a marked HN predilection (17/20), with a substantial proportion involving glandular sites. In contrast, HN ES arose in the skull base and sinonasal tract. ALES showed basaloid, epithelioid, or round cell morphology, with occasional palisading and rare squamous differentiation. Diffuse cytokeratin expression was present in all ALES, with frequent p40/p63 positivity, whereas ES showed only focal cytokeratin staining. Nodal metastases occurred in 9/20 ALES cases. EWSR1 rearrangement was identified in all ALES and ES cases, with FLI1 fusion identified in 18/20 ALES and 1/3 ES cases. With a mean follow-up of 60.6 months, outcomes varied by site: salivary gland ALES showed a more favorable course (4/5 in remission), whereas thyroid (6/8) and non-HN ALES (3/3) more often progressed. HN ES demonstrated poor outcomes. ALES is a distinct entity that frequently mimics carcinoma and extends beyond classic morphologic patterns. Site-specific differences observed in our study may aid in diagnosis; however, accurate recognition remains difficult, and a high index of suspicion at specific anatomical sites may be important for diagnosis and management.
papers.journal: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc

papers.title: Case Report: Veno-Arteriovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Management of Pheochromocytoma-Induced Cardiac Arrest in a Post-Partum Patient.
papers.abstract: A 34-year-old woman, 2 days post-partum, was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for management of hypertensive crisis and respiratory failure. An 18-cm left adrenal mass was found on computed tomography (CT), suspicious for a pheochromocytoma. After cardiac arrest, the patient was placed on veno-arteriovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-AV ECMO) given recurrent destabilizing arrhythmias. After successful ECMO decannulation, the patient underwent an uncomplicated resection of her adrenal mass. Although VA-ECMO has been used to support patients with pheochromocytoma, this appears to be the first published case describing the use of a V-AV configuration in the management of a complex cardiac arrest.

papers.title: Selpercatinib in Pediatric and Adolescent Patients With RET-Altered Solid Tumors: Safety and Efficacy Results From the Phase I/II LIBRETTO-121 Study.
papers.abstract: Selpercatinib, a highly selective oral RET inhibitor with CNS activity, has previously demonstrated durable responses and an acceptable safety profile in adults with RET-driven cancers. Consequently, the safety and efficacy of selpercatinib were investigated in pediatric/adolescent participants. LIBRETTO-121 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03899792) was a multicenter phase I/II trial of selpercatinib in participants age 0.5-21 years with advanced, RET-altered solid tumors. In phase I, the primary end point was safety, including dose-limiting toxicities. In phase II, the primary end point was objective response rate (ORR) as determined by independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1. Key secondary end points included ORR by investigator, duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, and pharmacokinetics. As of November 8, 2024, 36 participants age 2-20 years were treated with selpercatinib. Tumor types included RET-altered medullary thyroid cancer (MTC, n = 15), RET fusion-positive papillary thyroid cancer (PTC, n = 15), and other (n = 6). The most common treatment-emergent adverse events were diarrhea, nausea, elevated AST, pyrexia, abdominal pain, elevated ALT, headache, cough, and vomiting. No treatment discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events or new adverse drug reactions were observed. ORR by IRC was 53% (19/36; 95% CI, 36 to 70). For participants with MTC and PTC, ORR by IRC was 60% (9/15; 95% CI, 32 to 84) and 53% (8/15; 95% CI, 27 to 79), respectively. The 24-month DOR rate was 100% (95% CI, 100 to 100). Selpercatinib showed durable efficacy in pediatric/adolescent participants with RET-altered thyroid cancer and was well tolerated, supporting targeting of RET alterations in pediatric/adolescent patients.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology

papers.title: Survival over two decades in neuroendocrine neoplasms care.
papers.abstract: The incidence of gastro-entero-pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs) has increased, alongside novel therapies and care models. Whether these advances translated into improved survival is unclear. Population-based retrospective cohort study of GEP-NENs between 2000-2019. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed using time-to-event methods. Restricted cubic splines assessed non-linear associations between diagnosis year and hazards of death; multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, primary site, and metastatic status. Among 9,420 patients, 5-year OS was 75.8% overall, 88.8% for non-metastatic disease, and 57.0% for metastatic disease. Mortality risk declined in more recent years, with diagnoses in 2013-2019 associated with lower hazards of death (adjusted HR 0.91, 95%CI 0.83-0.99). Improvements were confined to non-metastatic disease and to pancreas, stomach, and rectal primaries. OS has modestly improved over two decades, largely reflecting stage migration rather than clear therapeutic gains. Advances that meaningfully improve survival in advanced GEP-NENs are needed.

papers.title: Actinomycetota-Derived Metabolites in Pancreatic Cancer: Chemical Diversity, Metabolic Vulnerability, and Translational Barriers.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains among the deadliest malignancies worldwide, and effective therapies are still lacking. Actinomycetota are among the richest microbial sources of bioactive secondary metabolites, and three agents in clinical use against pancreatic malignancy derive from them - streptozotocin, everolimus and doxorubicin - though all three are indicated for neuroendocrine rather than ductal tumors. This review provides a critical narrative synthesis of Actinomycetota-derived metabolites evaluated in pancreatic cancer models, with every potency value re-derived from the primary literature and interpreted alongside assay conditions and available mechanistic and in vivo evidence. Fifty-two compounds from 25 primary reports encompass polyketides, nonribosomal peptides, depsipeptides, RiPPs, alkaloids, ionophores and hybrid scaffolds. Rather than a simple ranking of increasingly potent cytotoxins, the literature poses a sharper question about selectivity. Two compounds are conditionally active: kigamicin D only under nutrient deprivation and BE-43547A2 only under hypoxia, exploiting the metabolic state that defines the disease rather than any intrinsic difference between malignant and normal cells. Both were recovered by screens built to detect that behavior, and neither has been shown to hold a therapeutic window in vivo. Separately, thiogochangamide B retains activity in gemcitabine-resistant models, while trienomycin A binds STAT3 directly, suppresses proliferation across eight pancreatic lines, achieves 84-98% tumor growth inhibition in xenografts at doses producing no detectable toxicity, and distributes preferentially to pancreatic tissue. Conditional activity is best read as a hypothesis about how such compounds should be sought rather than as an established route to selectivity. Despite remarkable chemical diversity, translation remains constrained by the limited use of normal-cell controls, predictive biomarkers and clinically relevant preclinical models. Screens conducted in nutrient-replete, normoxic monolayer culture will systematically miss compounds of this kind. Future efforts should prioritize compounds that exploit the metabolic liabilities of pancreatic cancer rather than pursuing greater cytotoxic potency.

papers.title: Circulating biomarkers in the diagnosis and management of neuroendocrine neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) comprise a broad family of tumours arising from the diffuse neuroendocrine system and endocrine glands, and vary widely in clinical behaviour ranging from indolent to highly aggressive. Established monoanalyte biomarkers including chromogranin A and NEN-derived hormones have clinical utility but some major limitations including non-specificity for tumour origin, variable sensitivity between NEN subtypes, inconsistent correlation with prognostic factors including metastasis, and can be falsely elevated in common non-NEN pathologies. The expansion of investigative NEN biomarkers through advancing omics technologies and computational methods holds potential to improve diagnosis, prognostication and aid therapy selection or trial allocation. This review will outline established and evolving NEN circulating biomarkers, and their roles in clinical practice.

papers.title: Laparoscopic Duodenum-Preserving Pancreatic Head and Neck Resection.
papers.abstract: The selection of surgical approaches for benign and low-grade malignant tumors of the pancreatic head and neck, such as serous cystadenomas, neuroendocrine tumors, and intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), has long been controversial. Traditional pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) is associated with substantial trauma and requires gastrointestinal reconstruction, which alters normal physiological structures. With a deeper understanding of pancreatic function and the advancement of minimally invasive techniques, duodenum-preserving pancreatic head resection (DPPHR) has gained increasing attention because it preserves the integrity of the duodenum and bile duct, better maintaining physiological conditions. However, this procedure imposes extremely high technical demands on surgeons, particularly when performed laparoscopically. Laparoscopic duodenum-preserving pancreatic head resection (LDPPHR) is frequently confronted with high risks of intraoperative bleeding and postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF). With proficiency in LDPPHR attained by the present authors and its indications extended to lesions of the pancreatic head and neck, the surgical workflow was optimized to reduce the incidence of complications. Under precise preoperative three-dimensional visualization planning and meticulous dissection guided by intraoperative ICG fluorescence and AR navigation, the anterior and posterior pancreaticoduodenal arterial arcades were preserved, and the pancreatic cut surface was reconstructed using a modified Blumgart pancreaticojejunostomy, so that curative tumor resection is accomplished while organ function is maximally preserved and patient outcomes are improved. This report is presented as a demonstration of the technical feasibility of completing each step of the protocol; its safety and effectiveness require evaluation in larger series.

papers.title: PRAME predicting outcome in uveal melanoma.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intra-ocular malignancy in adults and carries a high risk of metastatic disease, affecting approximately 50% of patients despite advances in local tumour control. PRAME (PReferentially expressed Antigen in MElanoma) has emerged as a marker for metastatic risk; however, evidence is largely derived from mRNA expression studies rather than routine immunohistochemistry (IHC). This study evaluates PRAME protein expression by IHC in a large UM cohort and examines its association with clinicopathological features and survival outcomes. A total of 403 UM cases were included. PRAME IHC was performed on tissue microarrays (TMAs) and/or whole tumour sections and scored as positive based on nuclear staining in >10% of tumour cells. Associations were assessed using chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests. Survival outcomes were analysed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models. PRAME positivity was identified in 5% of TMA cases and 40% of whole-section cases. On TMAs, PRAME expression was associated with worse overall survival (median 26 versus 50 months; p = 0.03) but not metastasis-free survival (MFS). In contrast, whole-section PRAME expression was strongly associated with shorter MFS (median 5 versus 20 months; p < 0.001) and worse overall survival (median 13 versus 52 months; p = 0.04). In multivariate analysis including age, American Joint Committee on Cancer stage and BAP1 status, whole-section PRAME positivity remained an independent adverse predictor of MFS (hazard ratio = 10.5, p = 0.002). PRAME IHC is a clinically meaningful prognostic biomarker in UM, particularly when assessed on whole tumour sections, where it provides strong independent prognostic information.
papers.journal: The journal of pathology. Clinical research

papers.title: Contemporary systemic therapy of medullary thyroid cancer.
papers.abstract: Medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) is a less common subtype of thyroid cancer, and it should be managed under the care of expert multidisciplinary teams. Based on the available literature, the role of systemic therapy for MTC has evolved over the past couple of decades in line with the rapid development in our understanding of the biology of this cancer. Despite the initial successes of selective RET inhibitors in achieving good responses and reasonable disease control, resistance eventually develops in most patients. There is an unmet need to develop newer therapeutic approaches for the management of MTC. This should happen through multicenter, international collaborative efforts given the rarity of this cancer.

papers.title: Non-invasive Imaging Modalities for Breslow Thickness Estimation in Melanoma: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Breslow thickness (BT) is the most important prognostic biomarker in cutaneous melanoma and directly influences surgical management, sentinel lymph node biopsy decisions and survival outcomes. Several non-invasive imaging modalities have been investigated for preoperative BT estimation; however, their relative performance and clinical applicability remain unclear. To evaluate the agreement between non-invasive imaging-derived and histopathologically measured BT and to compare the technical characteristics, diagnostic performance, and clinical utility of currently available imaging modalities for preoperative melanoma staging. A scoping review was conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to December 1, 2025. Original studies evaluating non-invasive imaging techniques for BT estimation in cutaneous melanoma were included. Imaging modalities assessed comprised dermoscopy, reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM), optical coherence tomography (OCT), ultrasound (US), multispectral imaging (MSI), photoacoustic techniques, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches. Ninety-two studies met the inclusion criteria. Dermoscopy provided indirect assessment of invasiveness, while RCM and OCT offered complementary microstructural information but limited direct thickness estimation. US, particularly high-frequency (≥20 MHz) and ultra-high-frequency (≥50 MHz) systems, showed the strongest and most consistent evidence for direct BT assessment, with correlation coefficients often exceeding 0.90 and high performance across clinically relevant thresholds. Nevertheless, performance varied across devices, probe frequencies, acquisition protocols, and operators, with frequent overestimation and reduced accuracy in selected subgroups (in situ and thin melanomas). MSI showed moderate-to-good classification performance, while photoacoustic techniques yielded promising results but limited to small cohorts. Evidence for MRI and SPECT was scarce. AI-based approaches achieved moderate-to-good predictive performance but did not consistently outperform experienced clinicians, with generalizability limited by dataset and methodological heterogeneity. US currently represents the most extensively validated and clinically applicable non-invasive modality for preoperative BT estimation. A hierarchical imaging approach appears most appropriate, with dermoscopy as the first-line diagnostic tool, RCM and OCT providing additional lesion characterization, and HFUS enabling complementary depth assessment in lesions strongly suspicious for melanoma. Emerging photoacoustic and AI-based approaches require further validation, while histopathology remains the reference standard for definitive diagnosis and BT measurement.

papers.title: Renal Neuroendocrine Tumor Mimicking Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Renal pelvic or peripelvic neuroendocrine tumors are rare and may radiologically mimic invasive upper tract urothelial carcinoma. A man in his 70s presented with two episodes of painless gross hematuria and lower urinary tract symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia. Computed tomography urography and magnetic resonance imaging showed a 3.1-cm enhancing mass centered at the right renal pelvis with apparent cortical invasion. However, flexible ureterorenoscopy showed intact urothelium, and renal pelvic wash cytology was negative. Upper tract urothelial carcinoma with parenchymal invasion was suspected, and single-port robot-assisted right nephroureterectomy with bladder cuff excision was performed. Histology revealed a well-circumscribed, well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor beneath intact renal pelvic mucosa, with negative margins and a Ki-67 index of 4.9%. Ten-month postoperative imaging showed no recurrence or metastasis. Submucosal renal neuroendocrine tumors should be considered when imaging suggests a renal pelvic mass but endoscopy shows no mucosal lesion.

papers.title: Unilateral mixed corticomedullary tumor of the adrenal gland with a synchronous contralateral pheochromocytoma: A case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: A 37-year-old man had two years of fatigue, weakness, and mood changes, initially misdiagnosed as depression. Workup showed hypertension, elevated urinary normetanephrine, elevated free cortisol, and suppressed ACTH. Imaging revealed bilateral adrenal masses (7.5 cm left, 4.7 cm right) with left adrenal vein thrombosis; MIBG scintigraphy showed bilateral uptake. After alpha-blockade, he underwent bilateral adrenalectomy. Inhibin positivity in the left mass's cortical region suggested a possible first-reported unilateral mixed corticomedullary tumor with synchronous contralateral pheochromocytoma, though entrapped cortical cells couldn't be excluded without further markers. Elevated Ki-67 and bilateral involvement warrant long-term follow-up and genetic evaluation.

papers.title: Isolated splenic metastases from colorectal carcinoma and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor: a report of two rare cases.
papers.abstract: Splenic metastases usually historically signal pre-terminal malignancy, arising amid widespread tumor dissemination and most often discovered at autopsy. Isolated splenic metastases without disseminated disease are exceedingly rare, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Recognizing these presentations is important as isolated splenic involvement may be amenable to definitive management in contrast to the poor prognosis associated with splenic spread. In this report, we present two patients with isolated splenic metastases. The first is an 83-year-old patient with splenic metastasis secondary to colorectal cancer. The second is a 29-year-old patient with splenic metastasis secondary to a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PNET), which, to our knowledge, may represent a novel incidence. Neither patient had evidence of disseminated disease at presentation. In this case report, we review the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of both cases, each of which demonstrate a favorable short-term outcome. These cases taken together show that isolated splenic disease, when identified in the absence of widespread metastasis, can be operatively and chemically managed with favorable short-term results. The PNET patient in particular broadens the recognized spectrum of primary tumor locations that can metastasize to the spleen in isolation. Further reports and longer follow-ups, however, are needed to identify the optimal management and longer-term prognoses.

papers.title: A staged combined parenteral and enteral nutritional support strategy in an elderly patient with non-small cell lung cancer, severe pneumonia, type II respiratory failure, and pre-existing malnutrition: a case report.
papers.abstract: Severe respiratory critical illness with multiple comorbidities poses substantial challenges to nutritional management. Malnutrition is common but often underrecognized, and the optimal nutritional strategy remains unclear in patients with concurrent malignancy and prior gastrointestinal surgery. This case report describes the clinical application of a staged combined parenteral nutrition (PN) and enteral nutrition (EN) strategy in an elderly patient with complex multimorbidity, aiming to illustrate a practical, dynamically adjustable approach to nutritional support in similar settings. A 79-year-old man with a history of gastric malignancy surgery was admitted with coma and dyspnea, and was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer, severe pneumonia, type II respiratory failure, and moderate malnutrition [body mass index (BMI) 16.9 kg/m2; Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS-2002) score 7; Subjective Global Assessment (SGA): moderate malnutrition]. A staged nutritional regimen combining PN and EN via a nasojejunal tube was implemented and dynamically adjusted over three phases based on his gastrointestinal tolerance and clinical evolution. During the intervention, white blood cell count (WBC) decreased from 22.90×109/L to 8.60×109/L and neutrophil percentage from 89.80% to 78.40%, indicating systemic inflammation control. Hemoglobin, total protein, and albumin initially improved but gradually declined with tumor progression. Oxygenation was maintained with peripheral oxygen saturation ≥98.4% under high-flow nasal oxygen after extubation. This case illustrates that in elderly patients with critical respiratory illness complicated by malignancy, prior gastric surgery, and malnutrition, a staged PN-EN combined strategy can be implemented with dynamic adjustments based on tolerance and clinical changes. However, sustained nutritional improvement may be limited by persistent tumor catabolism and disease-related stress. Nutritional support should be closely coordinated with antitumor and anti-infective therapies. The findings are observational and derived from a single case, and further research is needed to confirm broader applicability.

papers.title: Endobronchial Pulmonary Typical Carcinoid Tumors in Young Adults: A Three-Case Series Highlighting Obstructive Complications and Surgical Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Typical pulmonary carcinoid tumors are uncommon, well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms that often arise in the central airways and may present with nonspecific obstruction-related respiratory symptoms, resulting in delayed diagnosis. We report a three-case series of endobronchial typical pulmonary carcinoid tumors in young adults, highlighting their variable obstructive complications and surgical outcomes. This retrospective case series included three consecutive patients managed at a tertiary university hospital in Syria. Clinical presentation, imaging, bronchoscopic findings, operative details, histopathology, and follow-up data were obtained from medical records. All patients had histopathologically confirmed typical pulmonary carcinoid tumors with central/endobronchial involvement and underwent definitive surgical resection. Patient identifiers were removed, and written informed consent for publication and use of accompanying images was obtained. The patients were 23-35 years old and presented with different manifestations of central airway obstruction: chronic productive cough (Case 1), post-obstructive suppuration with lung abscesses (Case 2), and recurrent hemoptysis with atelectatic/post-obstructive changes (Case 3). Bronchoscopy demonstrated obstructing endobronchial lesions in all three cases, and histopathology confirmed typical carcinoid tumors with low mitotic activity and no necrosis. Case 1 underwent right middle and lower bilobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection for a large tumor staged T4N1M0. Cases 2 and 3 underwent left lower lobectomy; in Case 3, this included bronchial segment resection with primary closure and mediastinal lymph node dissection. Resection margins were negative in all cases, and mediastinal nodes were negative in Cases 2 and 3. No adjuvant therapy was administered. Follow-up showed no recurrence approximately 4.5 years after surgery in Case 1, clinical stability at one month in Case 2, and stable chest imaging at six months in Case 3. Endobronchial typical pulmonary carcinoid tumors in young adults can produce diverse obstruction-related complications, including chronic cough, post-obstructive suppuration, and hemoptysis with atelectatic changes. Timely airway evaluation and complete surgical resection with appropriate nodal assessment can achieve favorable outcomes, including in locally advanced disease when complete resection is feasible.

papers.title: Complete molecular response of left adrenal metastasis from pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor following stereotactic body radiation therapy: a case report.
papers.abstract: While pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNETs) often metastasize to the liver, adrenal gland involvement is uncommon. Management of adrenal metastases with stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is not common and outcomes are not well described. We report a case of metastatic PNET to the adrenal gland demonstrating sustained complete molecular response without anatomic resolution following SBRT within a multimodal treatment. A 48-year-old male patient was diagnosed in September 2023 with a well-differentiated grade 1 PNET. Initial imaging revealed an 8.9 cm centrally necrotic pancreatic tumor with diffuse peripancreatic infiltration and a biopsy proven 2.9 cm left adrenal metastasis. The tumor was somatostatin receptor (SSTR) positive (Krenning score 4) and was deemed surgically unresectable. Despite sequential treatment with capecitabine-temozolomide, followed by folinic acid, fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) and folinic acid, fluorouracil, and irinotecan (FOLFIRI), the adrenal lesion progressed, enlarging to 6.9 cm × 6.3 cm and demonstrated high-grade transformation to well-differentiated grade 3 (Ki-67 40%) by May 2025. The patient underwent SBRT to the left adrenal metastasis, receiving a total dose of 6,000 cGy in 5 fractions followed by systemic peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with 177Lu-DOTATATE for primary pancreatic disease control. One month after SBRT, post-treatment imaging demonstrated reduction in adrenal lesion size (4.5 cm × 4.0 cm) with complete absence of radiotracer uptake. Follow-up imaging in December 2025 confirmed continued size reduction and persistent absence of SSTR uptake. At nearly 1-year post-SBRT, a repeat 64Cu-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) scan showed no left adrenal gland hypermetabolic activity consistent with a sustained complete molecular response despite persistent residual lesion size. This case of metastatic PNET to the left adrenal gland achieved complete molecular response without anatomic resolution nearly 1-year following ablative SBRT within a multimodal treatment strategy. SBRT may represent an effective local control strategy and therapeutic bridge in carefully selected patients undergoing multimodal treatment.

papers.title: Endoscopic submucosal dissection for colitis cystica profunda in a 49-year-old woman: a case report with 52-month follow-up and sustained remission.
papers.abstract: Colitis cystica profunda (CCP) is a rare benign colorectal lesion characterized by mucus-filled cysts within the submucosa. However, the durability of endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for CCP beyond 48 months has not been documented. This case aims to fill that gap. ESD has emerged as a minimally invasive approach enabling both definitive diagnosis and treatment, but data on long-term efficacy remain limited, with no reported follow-up exceeding 48 months. A 49-year-old woman presented with a 6-month history of unformed stools. Colonoscopy revealed a submucosal mound-like lesion in the rectum, 5 cm from the anal verge. Endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) showed hypoechoic areas (0.4 cm × 0.2 cm) confined to the muscularis mucosa and submucosa, suspicious for a neuroendocrine tumor. Routine laboratory tests (complete blood count, C‑reactive protein, carcinoembryonic antigen) were within normal limits. ESD was performed for en bloc resection. Histopathological examination demonstrated cystica dilated glands in the submucosa lined by benign colonic epithelium with surrounding fibrotic stroma and chronic inflammatory infiltration, confirming the diagnosis of CCP. No cytologic atypia was observed. The patient was followed with serial colonoscopy at 12, 40, and 52 months post-ESD, and with contrast‑enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at 12 months. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Wexner Constipation Score (0/30) and 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) questionnaire (scores comparable to population norms). All follow‑up examinations showed stable scar‑like changes without evidence of recurrence, and the patient maintained normal bowel habits (formed stools 1-2 times daily). This case provides preliminary evidence that ESD can achieve durable remission and excellent functional outcomes in a single patient with CCP over 52 months. However, these findings are from one case and require confirmation in larger, prospective studies.

papers.title: Unusual paraneoplastic thrombocytosis in small bowel neuroendocrine tumor responding to 177Lu-DOTATATE.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are often associated with paraneoplastic features including carcinoid syndrome in up to 30% to 40% of cases. However, paraneoplastic thrombocytosis is a rare NET-associated condition. We report the case of a 59-year-old woman referred for significant and unexplained weight loss. Biological evaluation revealed thrombocytosis (900 × 109/L). A thoracoabdominal and pelvic computed tomography (CT) scan revealed multiple liver and bone lesions, suggestive of metastatic disease. Colonoscopic evaluation identified a well-differentiated NET as the primary tumor. Hematologic explorations revealed no underlying hematological condition explaining thrombocytosis. Cold somatostatin analogue treatment was started and resulted in initial stabilization of the disease. However, follow-up CT scan showed liver progression after 2 years concomitant with worsening thrombocytosis. 68Ga-DOTATOC positron emission tomography showed intense uptake of all known tumoral lesions; the patient was then treated with 177Lu-DOTATATE. Under 177Lu-DOTATATE treatment, platelet counts gradually decreased until normalization 8 weeks after the first injection, remaining within the normal range for up to 18 months, in parallel with clinical improvement. In conclusion, we report a rare case of paraneoplastic thrombocytosis associated with a small bowel NET showing rapid biological resolution from the first cycle of 177Lu-DOTATATE.

papers.title: Synchronous lung adenocarcinoma and pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets in different lobes: a case report.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets are small (< 5 mm) neuroendocrine proliferations that are usually identified incidentally in resected lung tissue. Their coexistence with a spatially separate lung adenocarcinoma is uncommon and may complicate the interpretation of multiple pulmonary nodules. A 71-year-old woman with multiple bilateral pulmonary micronodules that had remained radiologically stable for approximately 2 years was admitted after a newly detected lesion in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe was considered suspicious for lung cancer. She reported occasional chest tightness and intermittent cough with sputum and had never smoked. Bronchoscopy and brush cytology were negative. The patient underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left upper lobe lesion. Frozen-section examination showed adenocarcinoma, prompting a left upper lobectomy with systematic lymph-node dissection. A left lower lobe wedge resection was performed to sample representative micronodules. Final pathology showed a 3.0-cm invasive adenocarcinoma (approximately 80% acinar and 20% lepidic patterns), without visceral pleural, definite vascular invasion, or metastasis in 17 sampled lymph nodes (pT1cN0M0, stage IA3). The left lower lobe nodules were reported as pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets and were positive for AE1/AE3, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, CD56, and TTF-1, with a Ki-67 index of approximately 2%. The adenocarcinoma harbored an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. She was discharged 1 week after surgery. This case illustrates that pulmonary micronodules accompanying a dominant lung cancer may represent a separate neuroendocrine proliferation rather than intrapulmonary metastases. Diagnosis requires correlation of lesion size, morphology, and immunophenotype. Unsampled contralateral nodules could remain radiologically indeterminate and undergo structured surveillance.

papers.title: Primary Hepatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Systematic Review and Expert Pathologist Reappraisal Using the WHO 6th Edition Framework.
papers.abstract: Primary hepatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PHNENs) are exceedingly rare. Published evidence often lacks adequate clinicopathological support for a primary hepatic origin and uses inconsistent historical terminology. Previous reviews have pooled well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours (NETs), poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), and mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs), despite differences in biology, prognosis, and management. We systematically reviewed reported PHNENs using PRISMA-based screening and expert pathology reappraisal within the WHO 6th edition morphology-first framework. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were screened according to predefined eligibility criteria; eligible articles underwent second-level expert assessment of pathology, including morphology (including NET G3 vs. NEC and MiNEN vs. amphicrine carcinoma), immunohistochemistry (expression of at least two NE markers), proliferation (Ki-67/mitotic activity), as well as clinical/imaging work-up to exclude metastases from extrahepatic primaries. Of the 67 potentially eligible studies submitted to expert pathology-based reappraisal, 28 studies (49.1%) were retained in the final dataset with 57 likely NEN cases (mainly case reports/small case series). Among the 57 cases, most were well-differentiated NETs (78.9%); NECs (8.8%), MiNENs (3.5%), and amphicrine carcinomas (1.8%) were less frequent. Some cases were high-grade NENs that could not be distinguished as well or poorly differentiated (7%). PHNEN literature is constrained by rarity, uncertainty of hepatic origin, and historical misclassification. Future studies and registries should report a minimum diagnostic dataset with standardised terminology according to the WHO 6th edition framework and in-depth clinical/imaging studies.

papers.title: Analysis of Ocular Surface Tumours and Lesions by High-definition Anterior-segment Optical Coherence Tomography.
papers.abstract: High resolution AS-OCT (Anterior segment- Optical coherence tomography) is an imaging modality predominantly used in tertiary ophthalmologic centres to diagnose and characterise various ocular surface tumours as well as an adjunct to monitor treatment response. The objective of this study was to evaluate the utility of AS-OCT for ocular surface tumours. This was a prospective cohort study of patients done at a tertiary care hospital in Nepal over one year from 2023 August to 2024 July. A consecutive sampling was done in the patients aged 18 years and older who were suspected of having ocular surface tumours and lesions during the study period. Demographic data, slit lamp biomicroscopic examination including size, site and morphology of tumour and AS-OCT using High Definition Zeiss Cirrus 6000 were carried out for all patients enrolled. Diagnosis was based on clinical evaluation and AS-OCT features. Those patients suspected of malignancy surgical excision and their histopathology was analysed. Among the 110 enrolled patients, the median age was 50 (range: 18-87) years. Of them, 63 (57%) were female and 47 (43%) were male. A total of 5 (4.5%) participants had bilateral involvement. Based on clinical picture and AS-OCT features, 84 eyes (73.04%) were diagnosed to have ocular surface squamous neoplasia (OSSN), 18 eyes (15.65%) with conjunctival nevus and two eyes (1.73%) were suspected to have melanoma. Histopathology of 80 eyes who underwent surgical excision, OSSN of various grades in 86% eyes was the most common diagnosis followed by conjunctival melanoma in 3%. Though HPE is a gold standard for diagnosing ocular surface tumours, AS-OCT can provide a noninvasive optical biopsy. Additional research in AS-OCT is needed to increase the sensitivity and specificity of accurately diagnosing ocular surface lesions.

papers.title: Cutaneous melanoma and JAK inhibitors: a disproportionality analysis in EudraVigilance.
papers.abstract: Pharmacovigilance aims to ensure that the risk-benefit balance remains favourable throughout the entire life-cycle of drugs. Although JAK inhibitors have been associated with the development of skin cancers, melanoma is not mentioned in their data sheets, except in the case of tofacitinib. A case/non-case study was performed in EudraVigilance to evaluate the association between exposure to JAK inhibitors and the adverse reaction "skin melanomas(excluded ocular)" by calculating the reporting odds ratio. Additionally, univariate and multivariate analysis were performed to assess whether different variables could have an influence on melanoma development. Until April 30, 2025, the EudraVigilance database included 158 reports with tofacitinib, 65 with ruxolitinib, 42 with upadacitinib, 21 with baricitinib, 2 with filgotinib, and 1 with abrocitinib. The reporting odds ratio analysis showed a signal between exposure to baricitinib, ruxolitinib, tofacitinib, upadacitinib, and the explored adverse reaction. Besides, when analysing the association of malignant melanoma (the most frequently coded PT in individual case reports) with different variables, a statistically significant association was observed based on the drug(p = 0.0014) and the indication(p = 0.0037). In this EudraVigilance disproportionality analysis, signals of disproportionate reporting for cutaneous melanoma were identified for baricitinib, ruxolitinib, tofacitinib, and upadacitinib. These findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal association. Further evaluation in cohort studies, disease registries, and electronic health-record databases is required to confirm and quantify any potential association between JAK inhibitor exposure and melanoma. Given the seriousness of melanoma and the potential influence of confounding and surveillance bias, these results support maintaining clinical vigilance and appropriate dermatological monitoring in patients receiving JAK inhibitors, particularly those with additional melanoma risk factors.

papers.title: Perioperative chemotherapy and long-term cure in resected grade 3 gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine carcinomas: The GETNE SOUTH-NEC Study.
papers.abstract: In resected stage I-III gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine carcinomas (GEP-NEC), whether perioperative chemotherapy eradicates residual disease or merely delays relapse is unknown, since Cox models cannot distinguish these effects. We analysed 162 patients with resected stage I-III GEP-NEC from the GETNE registry. Event-free (EFS), recurrence-free (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were modeled by Cox regression with chemotherapy as a time-dependent exposure, adjusted for age, sex, performance status, stage, Ki-67 and site, and by a Bayesian promotion-time cure model that separates a clonogenic (cure) component from a kinetic (relapse timing) component. Seventy-four patients (46%) received chemotherapy; median follow-up was 93 months. Chemotherapy was associated with longer EFS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.61; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.40-0.96) and RFS (HR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.37-0.93), but not clearly with OS (HR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.46-1.15). On EFS, the cure model attributed the association to a lower clonogenic burden (ratio, 0.67; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.40-1.11; posterior probability, 94%) rather than to slower kinetics (ratio, 0.93); on RFS both components contributed. The population cure fraction was 22.7% (95% CrI, 15.9-29.6) for EFS and 28.6% (21.9-35.7) for RFS, matching the Kaplan-Meier plateaus. No Ki-67 by chemotherapy interaction was detected. In resected grade 3 GEP-NEC, perioperative chemotherapy is associated with longer EFS and RFS and, on the composite endpoint, with a higher probability of long-term cure rather than delayed recurrence. These associations are observational and the cure-versus-delay decomposition is descriptive. Cure models add information beyond conventional survival metrics.

papers.title: Development and Validation of a Model to Predict Recurrence in Patients With Stage IIIA Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Patients with stage IIIA cutaneous melanoma have relatively favorable prognoses (5-and 10-year overall survival probabilities of 93% and 88%, respectively), yet they are considered for systemic adjuvant therapy. Identifying the subset of patients at highest risk of recurrence could limit adjuvant treatment-related toxicity and direct therapy to those most likely to benefit. Patients aged ≥18 years with stage IIIA melanoma diagnosed between 2001 and 2016 at 36 centers, primarily in Europe and North America, were included in the study. The full cohort was split in a 3:1 ratio into development (n=1,386) and validation (n=448) cohorts. A random forest procedure was applied to the development cohort to select variables for inclusion. The selected variables were incorporated into a Fine-Gray model to predict recurrence-free survival and graphically represented as a nomogram. Model performance was assessed using the C-index and inspection of the calibration plot. The model's clinical utility was assessed using decision curve analysis and compared with alternative strategies. Eight variables were included in the model and were associated with the incidence of recurrence: mitotic rate (P<.001), number of positive sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs) per nodal basin (P<.001), diameter of the largest focus in the SLN (P=.001), ulceration (P<.001), age (P=.022), number of metastatic foci in the SLN (P=.019), lymphovascular invasion (P<.001), and extranodal extension (P=.005). In the validation cohort, the model had a C-index of 80.9% and appeared to be well calibrated. Decision curve analysis demonstrated a significant net benefit for adjuvant therapy guided by the nomogram compared with alternative strategies, including treating all patients with adjuvant therapy, treating no patients, or treating only patients with stage IIIA disease and >1.0-mm nodal tumor burden. Our prediction model can improve patient selection for adjuvant therapy compared with other available strategies.

papers.title: "Single-Centre Audit of Bone-Modifying Agents in Neuroendocrine Neoplasm Bone Metastases".
papers.abstract: Bone metastases in neuroendocrine neoplasms are uncommon but cause significant morbidity. A recent Italian survey of 320 patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms and bone metastases reported skeletal-related events in 23% and bone-targeted agent use in 31%, highlighting limited evidence for bone-modifying agents. We identified adults with confirmed or clinically suspected neuroendocrine bone involvement who received a bone-modifying agent at a UK tertiary centre (January 2019-September 2024), using institutional prescribing records. Demographic, tumour, treatment, and toxicity data were extracted from records. Twenty-two patients received treatment (denosumab 17 [77%], zoledronic acid 5 [23%]). Most (91%) had grade 1-2 tumours; 64% had gastro-entero-pancreatic primaries. Bone metastases were synchronous in 46% and widespread (more than three lesions) in 73%. At diagnosis, 22% were symptomatic; during follow-up, 78% developed pain, high blood calcium, or a skeletal-related event. Skeletal-related events, a composite of pathological fracture, spinal cord compression, radiotherapy to bone, or orthopaedic surgery, occurred in 41% (radiotherapy alone in 36%); pain-relieving medication was used universally. Treatment was mainly given every 12 weeks (median six doses). Low blood calcium occurred in 9% and osteonecrosis of the jaw in 5%; dental assessment before therapy was recorded in only 9%. These figures are broadly consistent with the Italian survey cited above. Treatment use was heterogeneous, reflecting a lack of disease-specific guidelines, and toxicity was comparable to other solid tumours and generally manageable. Our findings highlight the need for prospective studies and structured registries to clarify treatment use, dosing, and impact on quality of life and prognosis.

papers.title: [Real-world outcomes of avelumab treatment for Merkel cell carcinoma : An Austrian multicenter real-world study].
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare, aggressive neuroendocrine skin cancer. Treatment with avelumab (Programmed Death-Ligand 1 (PD-L1) antibody) is established in advanced disease, but real-world data are limited. To assess effectiveness and safety of avelumab for advanced MCC in Austria. This multicenter retrospective chart-review study included 49 patients with Merkel cell carcinoma who had received at least one cycle of avelumab between September 2017 and December 2023. The primary endpoint was real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS). Secondary endpoints included real-world overall survival (rwOS), real-world objective response rate (rwORR), real-world duration of response (rwDOR), real-world time to response (rwTTR), and safety; real-world time to treatment discontinuation (rwTTD) univariable subgroup analyses and post hoc multivariable Cox regression models were assessed exploratorily. Median rwPFS was 10.1 months (95% CI 1.8-18.4), and median rwOS was 22.9 months (95% CI 5.0-40.8). RwORR was 47.9% (95% CI 34.5-61.7), and median rwDOR was 19.2 months. Adverse events (AEs) occurred in 71.4% of patients and were grade ≥ 3 in 48.6% of affected patients. Immune- and/or treatment-related AEs were documented in 53.1%; 12.2% discontinued treatment due to adverse events. Real-world data support avelumab effectiveness with an expected safety profile in advanced MCC. In routine care, AEs may limit treatment duration, underscoring structured monitoring and interdisciplinary management.

papers.title: CRISPR-Cas9 screen identifies eIF4G2 as a regulator of CD8+ T cell dysfunction.
papers.abstract: CD8+ T cells directly target and kill cancer cells and are required for effective antitumor immunity. However, CD8+ T cells may become dysfunctional when exposed to chronic antigen stimulation during cancer. Dysfunction is characterized by reduced proliferation, increased expression of inhibitory receptors, and impaired effector function, yet the genetic mechanisms controlling dysfunction remain poorly understood. Therefore, we developed a murine ex vivo chronic stimulation model that recapitulates features of CD8+ T cell dysfunction observed within the tumor microenvironment. By coupling this system with genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 loss-of-function screening, we discovered that the progression of murine CD8+ T cells to a dysfunctional state required eIF4G2, a noncanonical mRNA translation factor. Deletion of eIF4G2 restored CD8+ T cell survival and proliferation during chronic stimulation conditions in vitro. Transcriptomic, proteomic, and flow cytometric analyses revealed that eIF4G2 deletion shifts CD8+ T cell phenotype from a dysfunctional state to a proliferative state. eIF4G2 depletion reduced oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and accumulation of misfolded protein aggresomes during chronic in vitro stimulation. Finally, eIF4G2-depleted cells mediated enhanced tumor control in a murine model of melanoma. These data suggest that targeting eIF4G2 may promote CD8+ T cell resilience and improve therapeutic antitumor immunity.
